What the Peel Keeps

The loop wall from hydrogen to astatine: Dirac Time, both meanings of VOTKP, and the element ledger

Jeromie Beasley
Version 1.2.3 · 23 November 2026

AI-assisted: the research direction, framework and questions are Jeromie Beasley’s; data passes were run with ChatGPT and Codex (OpenAI), and every number was rechecked against the archive with scripts, and the wall algebra and archive calls were formalised in Lean with Claude (Anthropic).

Abstract. I peel each atom one electron at a time and record every step as the ratio zz of successive removal energies, with reflection Γ=(z−1)/(z+1)=tanh(12lnz)\Gamma = (z-1)/(z+1) = \tanh(\tfrac12\ln z) on my Smith disc and two books E−=(ΔIE)2E^- = (\Delta IE)^2 and E+=(ΣIE)2E^+ = (\Sigma IE)^2 whose ratio is Γ2\Gamma^2. The loop wall Γ2=12\Gamma^2 = \tfrac12, at z=3+22=5.828427z = 3+2\sqrt2 = 5.828427, is derived, not fitted: it is where two equal faces at a right angle stop closing a loop, the point where their commutator becomes a single Jordan block, and the only equal-face cutoff for which the sum and product forms of the two-face rule agree. Run through every element from hydrogen to astatine, the wall sorts 3,570 ordinary steps so that exactly eight cross — lithium, beryllium, boron and carbon at the helium core, and sodium, potassium, rubidium and caesium at the neon, argon, krypton and xenon cores — and every core sequence crosses inward once and stays inside. At the anion rung the reflection is hardness over electronegativity, and the wall is exactly electrophilicity equal to hardness; 53 of 65 adopted anion rungs lie outside, and seven of eight heavy-anion calls written before the numbers agree, with polonium provisionally contradicted by preliminary laser fits. Every classification survives only for cutoffs between silver’s anion rung and silicon’s, 5.80790 to 5.86654, and the wall lies inside. Across the visible, all 35 metals with optical data reflect above the same half-power circle and none of the 6 non-metals do. The anion rung and the first core opening give each element an address in seven classes. My face apex tanh(lnz/4)\tanh(\ln z/4) is exactly the scale coordinate of orbital survival under a sudden change of Coulomb scale, and a signed same-charge reflection, anchored to a mass, predicts that holmium-163 and dysprosium-163 swap ground-mass order between 56+ and 57+. I register a prediction for francium — inside the wall if and only if its second ionisation energy is below 23.7377 eV — and set out the oxygen, hydrogen-like and optical settings that could separate the exact wall from its neighbours. The wall’s exact statements are certified in 271 Lean theorems with no Mathlib. The work joins Dirac Time, both readings of VOTKP, my ball and two-trees constructions, my intrinsic projector geometry and my connection-energy, offset, transport, rate and gravity papers in one record, and keeps every failed test at full size.

The question that connects the papers

My work began with questions about Walter Russell, Tesla and the periodic table, and my founding aim has always been to map and measure everything simply, the way light does. This paper brings that aim back to the periodic table. Peel an atom one electron at a time, record each step as a ratio of successive removal energies, and ask what the record of each peel keeps.

My starting point is an act of observation. Something passes a boundary. An observer keeps a record on one side and asks whether the next reading can be predicted from it. In Dirac Time, imposing a boundary condition changes which modes are admissible. In the element ledger, removing an electron changes which threshold comes next. In the ball work, energy can cross a junction while the clocks and walls on either side keep their identities. These operations share one question, and each has its own domain, units, admissible inputs and test.

HYPOTHESIS. “The vector determines the direction, that may be decay.” Whether the vector form has anything to do with space and volume, with light as the leader, I keep as an open question, not a claim. I take these statements literally enough to ask what has to be measured for each verb. An order on a sequence gives a direction of reading. A physical decay direction also needs specified parent and daughter states and an energy balance. A spatial volume needs enough independent directions and a definition of volume. A leading light field needs a controlled change in the field before a reproducible response. Each added assertion therefore has its own way to fail.

The answer this paper gives for the elements is a single number. A peel step with ratio zz has reflection Γ=(z−1)/(z+1)\Gamma = (z-1)/(z+1), and the step lies outside my loop wall when Γ2>12\Gamma^2>\tfrac12, that is z>3+22=5.828427z>3+2\sqrt2 = 5.828427. The wall is not fitted to the elements; it is where two equal faces at a right angle stop closing a loop. Run through every element from hydrogen to astatine, it sorts 3,570 ordinary steps so that only eight cross, and every one of the eight is the first opening of a closed noble-gas core.

Evidence key. MEASURED marks an experimental observation or experimentally derived source value, with its source; catalogued energies also carry their source grades, and theoretical and semiempirical entries keep those labels. DERIVED marks an implication of stated premises or the output of a stated computation; certificates about encoded numbers belong here. RECOGNISED marks an observed pattern, fitted relation or comparison still without an independent derivation. HYPOTHESIS marks a proposed physical meaning, mechanism or extrapolation. OPEN marks a question with its test named and not yet run. A test whose kill condition fired is marked as having failed this way: it failed in that setup, and the idea stays open for other setups. “Reported” means the cited work supplied the result; “rerun” means a computation done for this edition.

Scope. The two meanings of VOTKP in this paper are the Volume of the Knot Potential and the Vector of Traits Kept under Peeling. Calling them “volume” and “vector” names the constructions; it does not date the papers. The core sources are my own long forms, marked editions, notebooks and committed runs, and no substitute reconstruction of VOTKP supplies the definitions here. My numerics are computations on my own laptop, checked against other people’s published measurements.

The loop wall in my own geometry

Everything in this paper is read through one step and one number. A peel step takes an atom from one removal threshold to the next. I write the two positive energies as a=IEka = IE_k and b=IEk+1b = IE_{k+1} and keep three coordinates for the same step: z=ba,h=12lnz,Γ=z−1z+1=b−ab+a=tanhh.z = \frac{b}{a},\qquad h = \tfrac12\ln z,\qquad \Gamma = \frac{z-1}{z+1} = \frac{b-a}{b+a} = \tanh h . zz is the clock ratio, hh is the half-logarithm (the boost of the step), and Γ\Gamma is the reflection of the step on my Smith disc. The inverse is z=(1+Γ)/(1−Γ)z = (1+\Gamma)/(1-\Gamma). Fixing one threshold and the ordered reflections recovers every threshold connected to it, so nothing is lost except one overall scale. DERIVED (Lean: smith_identity, gam_inverse).

The midpoint and the two books

Write the same reflection a second way: Γ=(b−a)/2(b+a)/2=half the gapthe midpoint.\Gamma = \frac{(b-a)/2}{(b+a)/2} = \frac{\text{half the gap}}{\text{the midpoint}} . The still point of a step — the monad — sits exactly at the midpoint of the pair, and the reflection is how far each face reaches from it, measured in units of the midpoint. For the pair 3 and 7 the midpoint is 5, half the gap is 2, and Γ=2/5\Gamma = 2/5. I read this as Russell’s fulcrum: the still point between two opposed motions. DERIVED.

Squaring the two halves gives the two books of my connection-energy work: E−=(b−a)2=(ΔIE)2,E+=(b+a)2=(ΣIE)2,E−E+=Γ2.E^- = (b-a)^2 = (\Delta IE)^2,\qquad E^+ = (b+a)^2 = (\Sigma IE)^2,\qquad \frac{E^-}{E^+} = \Gamma^2 . E+E^+ is the positive book: the sum face. E−E^- is the negative book: the difference face, the record of the step. These are my two books. In Elizabeth Johnson’s notebook words they are “matter” (positive, the shell and its sections) and “memory” (negative, the recipe): the words are hers, the two books are mine. Every link in the chain carries both, and their ratio is the reflected power of the step. DERIVED. (Atlas card B189 holds E−/E+=Γ2E^-/E^+ = \Gamma^2; B207 holds the two books of one edge.)

Why the wall is where it is

The wall is not fitted to anything. It comes from asking when a loop made of two faces at a right angle can close. Give each face a boost hah_a, hbh_b and form the commutator of the two boosts taken at a right angle. Its trace is tr=2−4sinh2hasinh2hb.\operatorname{tr} = 2 - 4\sinh^2 h_a \,\sinh^2 h_b . The loop closes while the trace stays above −2-2 and opens below it. At the boundary, sinhhasinhhb=1\sinh h_a \sinh h_b = 1. Using sinh2h=Γ2/(1−Γ2)\sinh^2 h = \Gamma^2/(1-\Gamma^2) and writing u=Γa2u = \Gamma_a^2, v=Γb2v = \Gamma_b^2, the boundary condition uv=(1−u)(1−v)uv = (1-u)(1-v) reduces exactly to Γa2+Γb2=1.\Gamma_a^2 + \Gamma_b^2 = 1 . So the two-face test is Γa2+Γb2<1\Gamma_a^2 + \Gamma_b^2 < 1 (the loop closes) against Γa2+Γb2>1\Gamma_a^2 + \Gamma_b^2 > 1 (it opens), and the two forms sinhhasinhhb<1\sinh h_a\sinh h_b < 1 and Γa2+Γb2<1\Gamma_a^2+\Gamma_b^2<1 are the same statement. DERIVED (Lean: sinh_sq_form; two_face_identity in TwoFaceForms.lean).

With equal faces this gives the wall of one step: Γ2=12⇔z2−6z+1=0⇔z=3±22.\Gamma^2 = \tfrac12 \iff z^2 - 6z + 1 = 0 \iff z = 3 \pm 2\sqrt2 . The forward branch is z=3+22=5.828427…z = 3+2\sqrt2 = 5.828427\ldots; the reverse branch is its reciprocal. Multiplying 2Γ2>12\Gamma^2 > 1 by (a+b)2(a+b)^2 gives an exact integer test that never needs a square root: outside⇔2(b−a)2>(b+a)2.\text{outside} \iff 2(b-a)^2 > (b+a)^2 . DERIVED (Lean: wall_quadratic, wall_two_branches, outside_iff). In the two books the wall is E−=E+/2E^- = E^+/2: the difference book holds exactly half of the sum book.

Only this number makes the two forms of the rule agree

There are two natural ways to carry the equal-face threshold over to unequal faces. If the equal-face threshold were some other value Γ2=t\Gamma^2 = t, the sum form would read Γa2+Γb2<2t\Gamma_a^2 + \Gamma_b^2 < 2t, and the product form would read sinhhasinhhb<sinh2ht\sinh h_a \sinh h_b < \sinh^2 h_t, that is Γa21−Γa2⋅Γb21−Γb2<(t1−t)2.\frac{\Gamma_a^2}{1-\Gamma_a^2}\cdot\frac{\Gamma_b^2}{1-\Gamma_b^2} < \Big(\frac{t}{1-t}\Big)^2 . The identity (1−x)(1−y)−xy=1−(x+y)(1-x)(1-y) - xy = 1 - (x+y) shows that the two forms are one and the same test for every pair of faces exactly when t=12t = \tfrac12. For any other tt they disagree on some pair. The Lean file exhibits the disagreement concretely: at t=0.5005t = 0.5005 the pair x=0.9999x = 0.9999, y=0.0005y = 0.0005 is closed under one form and open under the other. So of the two named extensions, 3+223+2\sqrt2 is the only equal-face cutoff for which the rule does not depend on which extension you pick. DERIVED (Lean: two_face_identity, two_face_forms_agree, two_face_forms_split_at_midpoint in TwoFaceForms.lean; eleven theorems in BoundaryAgreement.lean prove the stronger all-threshold statement).

Direction is in the sign

Reversing the order of the two energies sends z↦1/zz \mapsto 1/z, h↦−hh \mapsto -h and Γ↦−Γ\Gamma\mapsto -\Gamma, and leaves Γ2\Gamma^2 unchanged. The sign of Γ\Gamma carries the direction of the peel; the wall test, which reads Γ2\Gamma^2, is blind to it. A ledger kept only in Γ2\Gamma^2 cannot tell the two orders apart. DERIVED (Lean: gam_reverse, power_even, reverse_same_side; the false control refute_power_odd is rejected). This is the first place where “the vector determines the direction” has an exact meaning: the direction lives in a signed quantity that the wall cannot see.

The face apex and the junction

A quarter-logarithm gives a fourth coordinate, the face apex: aapex=tanh(lnz4),Γ=2aapex1+aapex2,z=(1+aapex1−aapex)2.a_{\text{apex}} = \tanh\!\Big(\frac{\ln z}{4}\Big),\qquad \Gamma = \frac{2a_{\text{apex}}}{1+a_{\text{apex}}^2},\qquad z = \Big(\frac{1+a_{\text{apex}}}{1-a_{\text{apex}}}\Big)^2 . The apex is the reflection of the half-step z\sqrt z. At the wall, aapex=2−1a_{\text{apex}} = \sqrt2-1 and 1−aapex2=2(2−1)1-a_{\text{apex}}^2 = 2(\sqrt2-1). Two equal clocks facing each other across a junction give z=1z = 1 and Γ=0\Gamma = 0: a matched junction reflects nothing, however steep the ladder inside each atom. DERIVED (Lean: face_apex, matched_junction).

The loop at the wall: a single Jordan block

Take two equal steps along perpendicular directions as 2×22\times2 positive matrices B=exp(r2â⋅𝛔)B = \exp\big(\tfrac r2\,\hat a\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma\big), r=lnzr = \ln z — the spinor (Dirac) form of a step — and close the loop W=BiBjBi−1Bj−1W = B_iB_jB_i^{-1}B_j^{-1}. With R=Γ2R = \Gamma^2 the reflected share and T=1−Γ2T = 1-\Gamma^2 the transmitted share, trW=2−4sinh4r2=2−4(RT)2.\operatorname{tr}W = 2 - 4\sinh^4\!\tfrac r2 = 2 - 4\Big(\frac RT\Big)^2 . Below the wall WW is conjugate to a turn, cos(θ/2)=1−2(R/T)2\cos(\theta/2) = 1 - 2(R/T)^2: the walk is held. At Γ2=12\Gamma^2 = \tfrac12, trW=−2\operatorname{tr}W = -2, (W+1)2=0(W+1)^2 = 0 and W+1≠0W + 1 \ne 0 — one Jordan block, a full turn that cannot be undone by a rotation. At the threshold the peel-loop holonomy is parabolic up to sign; in the Lorentz representation it acts as a null rotation, fixing a lightlike vector. This is a statement about the loop, not about the signature of the projector metric or a physical spacetime light cone. Beyond the wall WW is a run. The obliqueness (my Petermann factor) K=1/(1−2Γ2)K = 1/(1-2\Gamma^2) blows up exactly at the wall. In Two Trees in One Ball (Theorem 5.3), when z>3+22z>3+2\sqrt2 the group generated by three perpendicular steps is Schottky — free and discrete, a tree. At the wall itself the loop is the Jordan block, which is why the boundary case is stated on its own. Steps on opposite sides of the wall pair up as ΓΓ′=12\Gamma\Gamma' = \tfrac12: ratios 5 and 7 give Γ=2/3\Gamma = 2/3 and 3/43/4, whose product is one half. DERIVED (VOTKP v3.3 §25.1; Two Trees in One Ball, Theorem 5.3; Non-normality v15 §5, where the wall is the non-zero nilpotent point of a real traceless 2×22\times2 operator).

These boosts act in the peel chart, the Poincaré-ball model of my peel coordinate. They are not boosts of a spacetime, and nothing here introduces one.

Where this lives in my geometry

My Smith disc is not a borrowed engineering chart. The map z↦Γ=(z−1)/(z+1)z\mapsto\Gamma = (z-1)/(z+1) is the Cayley map of the right half-plane onto the unit disc. The reflection coefficient an electrical engineer reads off a transmission line is the same coordinate, which is why I use the Smith chart as a working tool. Reflections of successive steps compose by my addition law u⊕v=(u+v)/(1+uv)u\oplus v = (u+v)/(1+uv), so the reflection of a multi-step peel is the ⊕\oplus-sum of its single-step reflections, and lnz=2artanhΓ\ln z = 2\operatorname{artanh}\Gamma is a hyperbolic length in the peel chart (VOTKP v3.3, Theorem 15.1 and Corollary 15.2). The wall sits at the length ln(3+22)=2ln(1+2)=1.7627\ln(3+2\sqrt2) = 2\ln(1+\sqrt2) = 1.7627. The same number is the two-level population-gap point tanh(βΔ/2)=1/2\tanh(\beta\Delta/2) = 1/\sqrt2 of Dirac Time §12.6 — a structural match between two of my papers, not an identity of mechanisms.

The intrinsic geometry is a different object again. On the projector bundle my Intrinsic Quantum Geometric Tensor is QΠ(A,B)=Tr(ΠA†B)=g−i2ΩQ_\Pi(A,B) = \operatorname{Tr}(\Pi A^\dagger B) = g - \tfrac i2\Omega, with metric g=12Tr(VW)g = \tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(VW) and Berry curvature Ω\Omega, bounded by |Ω|≤2gVVgWW−gVW2|\Omega|\le 2\sqrt{g_{VV}g_{WW} - g_{VW}^2}. Its metric is positive on every nonzero tangent, g(V,V)=12∥V∥HS2>0g(V,V) = \tfrac12\|V\|_{HS}^2 > 0, and no spacetime metric enters and none is substituted anywhere in this paper. The hyperbolic length lnz\ln z is a distance in the peel chart, not the intrinsic metric. The bridge between the two is the weight between two projector blocks, EB=∥PH(1−P)∥F2=12∥[H,P]∥F2E_B = \|PH(1-P)\|_F^2 = \tfrac12\|[H,P]\|_F^2 (The Weight Between; Universal Projector Geometry). On one peel edge this weight between and the edge’s connection energy are two rungs of the same coupling — the weight between at rung 0 of the gap-power ladder of The Weight Between, the connection energy at rung 2 — not one number.

In my ball picture each junction has a face at distance h=r/2h = r/2 from the cell centre. Its boundary circle has angular radius α\alpha with cosα=Γ\cos\alpha = \Gamma, so at the wall the face boundary reaches exactly 45∘45^\circ. In the gravity ledger the same rule is a positivity licence: the matrix (1ww‾1)\begin{pmatrix}1 & w\\ \bar w & 1\end{pmatrix} with w=Γa+iΓbw = \Gamma_a + i\Gamma_b is positive exactly when Γa2+Γb2≤1\Gamma_a^2+\Gamma_b^2\le1 (The Ledger Outlives the Metric, final edition v3, Theorems 1 and 5 (Theorems 3 and 5 in edition 6)). And because Γ\Gamma is a ratio, it is unchanged when every energy is multiplied by one constant — the scale invariance K↦cKK\mapsto cK of Matter at a Scale — which is why one threshold can be compared across all the elements.

The rest of this paper reads atoms, knots, balls, light and decay through these coordinates, and asks in each case which of them the observation actually keeps.

A criterion for what the observer can keep

DERIVED. Let a finite-dimensional state obey ẋ=Lx\dot x = Lx, let RR be a fixed linear observation, and let y=Rxy = Rx. An autonomous linear equation ẏ=My\dot y = My for all initial states exists exactly when LkerR⊆kerRL\,\ker R \subseteq \ker R. Indeed RL=MRRL = MR implies the inclusion. Conversely, define M(Rx)=RLxM(Rx) = RLx on the image of RR; it is well defined because two lifts differ by a vector in the invariant kernel. Extending MM to a complement has no effect on an observed state. A perturbation that stays invisible to the observation for all times lies in ⋂j=0d−1ker(RLj)\bigcap_{j=0}^{d-1} \ker\!\big(RL^{j}\big) for a dd-dimensional state; the power series and the Cayley–Hamilton identity prove it. An instantaneous record and a complete time trace can keep different information.

Split the state into a retained part uu and a hidden part vv, with generator blocks A,B,C,DA, B, C, D. Direct integration gives u̇(t)=Au(t)+BetDv(0)+∫0tBe(t−s)DCu(s)ds.\dot u(t) = A\,u(t) + B\,e^{tD}\,v(0) + \int_0^t B\,e^{(t-s)D}\,C\,u(s)\,ds . The hidden initial condition and the return through the hidden state both matter. The corresponding resolvent correction is B(ζI−D)−1CB(\zeta I - D)^{-1}C wherever that inverse exists. This fixes which memory term I am asserting: a static threshold table by itself supplies none of the four generator blocks.

A smaller check shows why the lost information matters for operator-valued traits. Let JJ include the retained orthonormal subspace, Q=I−JJ†Q = I - JJ^\dagger, and A=A†A = A^\dagger. Then J†A2J−(J†AJ)2=(QAJ)†QAJ.J^\dagger A^2 J - \big(J^\dagger A J\big)^2 = (QAJ)^\dagger\, QAJ . For the two-state swap and a one-coordinate observation, the retained AA is zero and the retained A2A^2 is one. This is a falsifier for any rule that multiplies compressed observables without auditing the hidden return. The record closes under this square precisely when QAJ=0QAJ = 0.

RECOGNISED. This criterion gives my programme one standard of evidence. For each proposed reduction I exhibit the retained map and look for two admissible states with identical retained values. If their target readings differ, extra data are necessary. The same reasoning applies to a knot mirror, a pair of differently normalised ladders, a phase-erasing projector or an isotope change. The witness has to be built inside the domain of the particular claim.

QAJQAJ is the off-diagonal block that couples what is kept to what is eliminated, and (QAJ)†QAJ(QAJ)^\dagger QAJ is the weight carried across that cut — the weight between of The Weight Between. It is never negative, and it vanishes only when nothing leaks. The same block returns below as the second book of the peel (see Projectors give a second book).

What Dirac Time contributes to the element paper

I began with a question about memory. Suppose two preparations have the same description now. Can anything I am allowed to do next tell them apart? My long form uses this question to separate a record, a way to read it, and a physical claim about its carrier. It gives the element programme a way to decide when keeping one more trait — a sign, an interior branch, a second probe — has actually gained information. It also keeps my original motivation: “No core ever. Memory first.” In the atomic tables, core names a specified electron configuration reached by successive removals. That is a different operational meaning from the philosophical phrase in the long form, and I keep the two apart.

The primary texts are the complete 101-page The Dirac Time of the Gigantefermion, long form v3.0.1 (25 September 2026, on Zenodo 26 September), and the 6 November v3.1 package. The later edition sharpens the chiral hypotheses and adds the Smith coordinate in §17.1. Citations below use v3.0.1 unless v3.1 is named, and the original section and theorem identifiers let a reader recover every hypothesis and figure in the originals.

Memory before clock, §§0–4

§0, Research lineage. One chiral object, two phase rails, one flow, hierarchical memory. These are four different commitments. The object is conjectural; the rails need calibrated readouts; a common flow needs a rank condition and compatible generators; and the hierarchy consists of specified record maps. Earlier calculations displaced the proposed generic codimension-one zero walls of the flat torus and the identification of full signed spectral flow with the universal clock. I keep the questions and the failed tests.

§1, Memory Before Clock. Write down what is observed, the future operations admitted, and which outcomes distinguish two preparations. An invariant can distinguish objects at one instant. A history records an ordered path. A hidden present distinction earns the name predictive memory only when it can affect an admitted future observation. For elemental work, identical first and final thresholds give two common observations. Distinct intermediate ladders are distinguishable records if the corresponding intermediate ions can be prepared and interrogated. A claim of material memory would further need histories prepared at matched endpoints and an observed later difference.

§2, The Exact Predictive Quotient. In a finite-dimensional linear state space of dimension dd, with one fixed evolution LL and observation RR, set 𝒪dv=(Rv,RLv,…,RLd−1v),N∞=⋂n≥0ker(RLn)=ker𝒪d.\mathcal O_d v = \big(Rv,\ RLv,\ \dots,\ RL^{d-1}v\big), \qquad N_\infty = \bigcap_{n\ge 0}\ker\!\big(RL^{n}\big) = \ker \mathcal O_d . Cayley–Hamilton gives finite termination, and LL preserves N∞N_\infty. The quotient has dimension rank𝒪d\operatorname{rank}\mathcal O_d, and every sufficient linear summary must have at least this rank. The present record alone closes exactly when LkerR⊆kerRL\ker R\subseteq\ker R, equivalently when RL=ARRL = AR for a descended evolution on the record space. Peel ladders with changing ionic charge and preparation protocols have not yet been given that fixed linear model; the theorem names the evidence needed for the stronger claim of minimal memory.

§3, What Transport Keeps. Successive declared reductions produce nested kernels for their compositions. Survival under transport, detectability by a particular probe, and effect on a later response answer separate questions. A finite list of traits can survive a reduction even when the chosen readout cancels.

§4, Why Dirac. The spinor (Dirac) operator and its spectral projectors give concrete meanings to orientation and transport. My proposed elementary knot-like electron adds a problem of field realisation, stability and sources.

The operator, the probe and the clock, §§5–9

§5, Chiral Negative Control and Projector Orientation. In a flat-torus block write a=m+αa = m+\alpha, b=n+βb = n+\beta and ϕ=arg(a+ib)\phi = \arg(a+ib). The eigenvalues of 2π(aσ1+bσ2)2\pi(a\sigma_1 + b\sigma_2) are ±2πa2+b2\pm 2\pi\sqrt{a^2+b^2}. The positive projector away from zero is (I+cosϕσ1+sinϕσ2)/2(I + \cos\phi\,\sigma_1 + \sin\phi\,\sigma_2)/2. A circle about the degeneracy holds the two eigenvalues fixed and gives spinor holonomy −1-1. For the fixed-domain self-adjoint Fredholm family with fixed chiral involution, the long form states when full spectral flow, eta and odd traces cancel. Projector probes can still read direction. At a zero mode one must use P−=I−P+−P0P_- = I - P_+ - P_0. The sign change of the elemental reflection under exchange of two energies is an elementary algebraic analogue. Physical mirroring, changing a spinor branch and reversing a peel order each need their own involution.

§6, Intrinsic Quantum Geometric Tensor. On a smooth patch of fixed-rank orthogonal projectors, a tangent V=V†V = V^\dagger has only cross-block parts in the PP, I−PI-P split. I form QP(V,W)=Tr(PV†W),gP(V,W)=12Tr(VW).Q_P(V,W) = \operatorname{Tr}\!\big(P V^\dagger W\big), \qquad g_P(V,W) = \tfrac12 \operatorname{Tr}(VW). Positivity, curvature control and unitary covariance are proved on this patch. A spectral gap enters a projector derivative through each coupled pair across an isolated cluster, with weights proportional to |Ḣmn|2/(En−Em)2|\dot H_{mn}|^2/(E_n-E_m)^2. This tensor lives on the projector bundle and is intrinsic. It is not a spacetime metric, and I do not substitute one for it anywhere in this paper. Ionisation energies compare binding thresholds across particle-number sectors. Importing the projector formula for those scalar differences needs the operators, couplings and joint state space to be specified. My broader non-normal framework can keep a contour ledger across the failure of a local tangent description.

§7, Gauge Phase, Aharonov, and Conditional Measurement. Wilson holonomy compares paths; a geometric phase needs a cyclic state history; ABL probabilities and weak values need a preparation, an instrument and a post-selection. For a normalised preparation and pure post-selection, p0|Aw|2≤⟨A2⟩p_0|A_w|^2 \le \langle A^2\rangle. The retained history, the conditional signal, its probability and the finite pointer displacement should each be reported separately.

Equal-endpoint histories can erase later signals. Finite-meter backaction can explain an apparent history signal. A reduced arrow can lack an irreversible mechanism. Boundary data can determine the proposed hidden record. A target field class can lack a stable finite-energy solution. Matter, field and boundary angular momenta may fail to close. A gravity proposal can lack a covariant source map and independent observables. Each outcome has a named scope.

What the two VOTKPs ask of one record

My starting question was whether a polynomial could tell me the volume around a knot. The later name, Vector of Traits Kept under Peeling, changed the question productively. What operation was performed, which traits survived it, and what would a second observer need in order to recover a trait the first one lost? The element work supplies a particularly clean instance. Electron removal leaves the nuclear charge fixed, changes the electronic state, and changes the energy of the next removal. The knot work supplies an instance in which different objects agree under several powerful tests. A common reading is possible because the operations, the retained quantities and the failures of recovery can all be named. There is still no map assigning a particular knot complement to a given element, or identifying its hyperbolic volume with an atomic volume. (Vector v2.9, §§1–3, 10–17; Volume, §§1, 6, 12–13.)

Both meanings of VOTKP stay in play, because I believe the two together are the key to mapping each element: the Volume of the Knot Potential asks what geometry an object carries, and the Vector of Traits Kept under Peeling asks what survives each removal.

A polynomial that actually keeps decay and direction

A real shift V0↦V0+π2V_0\mapsto V_0+\pi^2 making exactly one positively oriented turn fixes λ=2i/π\lambda = 2i/\pi; the other orientation reverses the sign. With the positive convention, |uρ|=e−2Vol(ρ)/π,arguρ=−2CS(ρ)/π(mod2π).|u_\rho| = e^{-2\,\mathrm{Vol}(\rho)/\pi},\qquad \arg u_\rho = -2\,\mathrm{CS}(\rho)/\pi \pmod{2\pi}. The modulus carries decay (volume) and the phase carries direction (Chern–Simons): that is why I call it the decay–direction polynomial. The Chern–Simons computation on 454 runs in §5 checks a congruence modulo π2/2\pi^2/2. A shift by that smaller period changes the sign of uρu_\rho, so a matched lift modulo π2\pi^2, or a sign-independent observable such as uρ2u_\rho^2, is needed before using such a computation to validate an individual phase. Squaring also discards phase information. (Volume, §§5–6.)

For the two non-abelian figure-eight geometries, with signed volumes ±2.02988…\pm2.02988\ldots and Chern–Simons zero, P41(x)=x2−2cosh(2⋅2.02988…/π)x+1≃x2−3.91567x+1.P_{4_1}(x) = x^2 - 2\cosh\!\big(2\cdot2.02988\ldots/\pi\big)\,x + 1 \simeq x^2 - 3.91567\,x + 1 . This uses the stated two-root family. For a family containing the complex-conjugate holonomy with the opposite signed volume and the same Chern–Simons class, the partner of uu is 1/u‾1/\bar u; that conditional statement needs a conjugation-closed set and compatible lifts. The database’s named exterior and the diagram exterior have opposite handedness in 42 of the 79 signed comparisons. The geometric-top-root check succeeded in 79 of 79 knots at its tolerances, and a three-drawing spectrum check in 13 of 13. Neither count supplies the complete spectrum for every knot. (Volume, §6.)

The torus phase convention gives directions −k2/(pq)(mod1)-k^2/(pq) \pmod 1. Every phase of that form is a pqpq-th root of unity. DERIVED qualification. The product over distinct such phases divides xpq−1x^{pq}-1 over ℂ\mathbb C. The geometry-indexed polynomial can repeat a phase, and divisibility of that polynomial needs a no-collisions proof because xpq−1x^{pq}-1 has simple roots in characteristic zero. In the source’s search, T(3,4)T(3,4) and T(3,5)T(3,5) gave one direction each, with three and four expected components. The hyperbolic figure-eight shape polynomial s2−s+1s^2 - s + 1 defines ℚ(−3)\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3}); its arithmetic field label belongs to that algebraic object. (Volume, §§6, 13.)

Where the polynomial enters the element results, and where it does not yet. The polynomial’s own tests on knots — the geometric top root on 79 of 79 knots and the three-drawing spectrum on 13 of 13 — are in Volume v1 §6. The decay–direction polynomial is meant as a knot invariant; so far the evidence is that three drawings give the same spectrum on 13 of 13 knots, which is not yet a proof. It enters this paper through the knot-side tests of what a scalar keeps and loses, and through its modulus–phase split, which I read as an analogue of the split the peel makes between Γ2\Gamma^2 (what the wall reads) and the sign of Γ\Gamma (direction). It does not yet enter any elemental classification: no element is assigned a knot. The nearest element-side knot facts are these. Cyclooctaselenium’s eight bonds form an unknot, so every finite collection of such rings admits disjoint discs; my representation product still needs a representation set before it can read the selenium control. The screw paths of β-manganese, trigonal selenium and tellurium carry a signed volume χ\chi that does not change under path reversal and flips under a mirror — the opposite law to Γ\Gamma (see Direction: the even half and the odd half). OPEN.

Additional crossings between the books

RECOGNISED in the knot census. A Jones polynomial evaluated along the unit circle supplies a climb, measured by its Mahler measure, and a turn, measured by normalised signed area. On 2,970 knots through twelve crossings the rank correlation is 0.8541 between climb and complement volume and −0.9335-0.9335 between signed turn and signature. The corresponding correlations with Chern–Simons are −0.031-0.031 and +0.053+0.053. Among 9,985 thirteen-crossing knots the climb–volume correlation is 0.8542. This is exactly where the new potential polynomial earns its place: a simpler invariant already remembers much about size and sense of turn while doing poorly on the particular phase the new polynomial encodes. (v3.3, §28.4.)

My original HOMFLY test is even more diagnostic. Sampling both variables on a unit torus gave correlation 0.036. Along the 𝔰𝔩N\mathfrak{sl}_N slices v=t−N/2v = t^{-N/2}, z=t1/2−t−1/2z = t^{1/2} - t^{-1/2}, the climb–volume correlations are 0.60 for N=0N = 0 (Alexander), 0.86 for N=2N = 2 (Jones), and 0.78–0.86 for N=3N = 3 through 8, on 12,955 knots. Using the slices and the log determinant gave R2=0.838R^2 = 0.838 against 0.795 for Jones and log determinant. These are empirical correlations that depend on where in the polynomial the reading is taken. The NN indexing a HOMFLY specialisation and the colour indexing representations in a coloured Jones sequence are different indices. (Volume, §7.)

The separate θ\theta computation found 78 zero rows in a census of 12,965 and 12,887 non-zero. Of 865 mutant groups, 682 were fully separated at the chosen common evaluation point, 38 partly separated and 145 unresolved. Agreement on sampled points leaves functional equality open. The first mirror evaluator missed a term on the trefoil and stopped at its calibration test; the repaired one gave zero for 35 of 35 mirror sums and non-zero for 35 of 35 same-hand controls across its tested two-strand torus examples. The mirror-sensitive quantity here is a knot invariant evaluated under a definite operation. An optical phase, a signed peel, a knot signature and the sign of a spatial chirality observable each need their own transformation rule. (v3.3, §28.5.)

Optical comparisons in the Volume paper. The complex optical coordinate there is (1−N)/(1+N)(1-N)/(1+N) for the chosen incident convention — the same Smith form, with the complex index in place of the clock ratio. Its visible average of squared modulus separates all 35 metals from all six non-metals in that optical dataset; I take this up as the colour line in Colour and the half-power line. The source reports that phase gaps predict thin-film colour differences among 39 pairs similar in bulk, with rank correlation 0.64. Absorption, film preparation, spectral averaging and substrate enter this coordinate; substituting an isolated-atom peel into the optical classification would quietly change the input and the detection condition. In the finite-film closure test a frozen reflection threshold (|Γ|=0.856|\Gamma| = 0.856, 171 film cases) scored 87%, with an explicit thickness interval and bump tolerance; a later threshold with higher in-sample accuracy belongs in the exploratory ledger. (Volume, §9; Vector v2.9, §§6–7.)

The surfaceology passage checks cross-ratio identities and hidden zeros in specific amplitudes, then adopts the strategy of locating zeros before deforming a record. The electron passage points to the shared group SL(2,ℂ)SL(2,\mathbb C) of spin representations and lifted hyperbolic holonomy. Neither supplies a functor from an atomic state to a knot representation. The molecular section gives the most direct stress test of the material reading: five of six privileged knots are torus knots in the list it uses, and the exception, the figure-eight, has a hyperbolic complement. I keep that exception even though the abstract of the Volume paper uses broader language. A physical molecular selection mechanism would have to explain the exception and separate synthesis route, template and topology. (Volume, §§8, 10–12.)

Where the synthesis could fail

Candidate identification Decisive check and present status
A scalar topology fingerprint determines complement volume Exhibit equal scalar fingerprints and unequal volumes. The October paper supplies examples and follows them to higher colours, the A-polynomial and representation windows. What remains is which richer data determine which geometry.
The scalar peel determines the path of a retained subspace Rotate eigenspaces at fixed spectral gaps. The record of scalar steps stays the same while projector motion can change. A dynamical lift needs its own hypotheses and initial state.
One ionisation coordinate controls line colour, reflection and refraction Define these as separate outputs. The optical film receiver keeps thickness and complex response. A Snell rule for filling order failed this way in §9. A visible ground-state line answers the different question of §27.
Charge-and-channel information for xenon has already closed the loop to memory Match the same charge, channel, energy, preparation and timing observable, with its uncertainty. The October text keeps the route to such a test; it reports no fitted element-specific kernel or extracted delay spectrum from thresholds alone.
A molecular knot identifies an isolated element with that knot Require an atom-to-invariant map and an independently measurable consequence. The molecular examples constrain realisations of chains and ligands, with exceptions to simple torus preferences. No element-by-element vacuum volume follows yet.
Light leads and the vector creates space or volume Specify a preparation, an intrinsic clock or phase observation beyond the energy ratios, its predicted change under a controlled intervention, and a comparison after matching the ratios. This remains my physical hypothesis.

(Vector v2.9, §§3, 6, 9–21; Volume, §§7–13; Vector v3.3, §§25–29.)

Building the ball from a directed step

I want to know what can be kept when the description of a system changes. The ball work gives that question an experimental meaning. Give each face a clock, connect two faces, and ask what reaches the next cell, what remains in the gap, and what survives a reversal. In my physical picture the nucleus is the centre, the cloud supplies the wall, and small electron balls form the ground between distinct walls. One ball breathing out and its neighbour taking up the disturbance is the mechanism I propose. Two balls pushed together connect at certain levels but always leave a layer of gap, and I read that gap as the spacing, angles and connections of the crystal lattice. Light leads, the wall acts as a critical angle, and the forced gap is what I call my Snell’s law at the hypersurface and Pauli exclusion. In the executable models, a clock, a port, a transmitted amplitude and a detector reading are four different objects. Keeping their names attached to their equations is how I find out which parts of the picture the experiments actually test.

DERIVED. An assigned positive clock ratio zz gives three coordinates, r=logz,a=tanh(r/4),Γ=tanh(r/2)=2a1+a2.r = \log z,\qquad a = \tanh(r/4),\qquad \Gamma = \tanh(r/2) = \frac{2a}{1+a^2}. The inverse is z=[(1+a)/(1−a)]2z = [(1+a)/(1-a)]^2. A face apex and an interface reflection both recover the same clock, by different maps. The example z=3z = 3 has a=2−3a = 2-\sqrt3 and Γ=1/2\Gamma = 1/2. Four aligned directed steps of this size have total logarithmic increment 4log34\log 3, equivalent ratio 81 and equivalent reflection 40/4140/41. That calculation prescribes a sequence of clocks. A wave at a specified frequency crossing four finite gaps also gathers phases, and predicting the transmitted intensity needs those phases and the boundary conditions. A length written as logz\log z is dimensionless until a length scale is supplied.

The face apex has an exact one-electron meaning

The quarter-logarithm in the apex turns out to be exactly the coordinate of a textbook atomic process. Take a sudden change between two same-centre Coulomb Hamiltonians with the same mass, and let α\alpha and β\beta be their inverse length scales. For a fixed orbital label the binding-energy ratio is z=(β/α)2z = (\beta/\alpha)^2, and a=tanh(lnz4)=β−αβ+α.a = \tanh\!\Big(\frac{\ln z}{4}\Big) = \frac{\beta-\alpha}{\beta+\alpha}. Put t=1−a2t = 1-a^2. Direct orbital integration gives the squared overlaps — the probabilities of finding the electron still in the same-label orbital after the change — P1s=t3,P2s=t3(1−3a2)2,P2p=t5.P_{1s} = t^3,\qquad P_{2s} = t^3\,(1-3a^2)^2,\qquad P_{2p} = t^5 . For 1s the overlap is 8(αβ)3/2/(α+β)38(\alpha\beta)^{3/2}/(\alpha+\beta)^3, whose square is exactly (1−a2)3(1-a^2)^3. At charge doubling, z=4z = 4, the three probabilities are 512/729=70.23%512/729 = 70.23\%, 2048/6561=31.21%2048/6561 = 31.21\% and 32768/59049=55.49%32768/59049 = 55.49\%. At the wall itself, a=2−1a = \sqrt2-1, each face keeps t=2(2−1)≈0.828t = 2(\sqrt2-1) \approx 0.828, and P1s=8(2−1)3=8(52−7)≈56.85%,P2s≈13.39%,P2p≈39.02%.P_{1s} = 8(\sqrt2-1)^3 = 8(5\sqrt2-7)\approx 56.85\%,\qquad P_{2s}\approx13.39\%,\qquad P_{2p}\approx39.02\% . Equal energy ratios can therefore put survival on opposite sides of one half depending on the orbital. Summing over all bound final states answers a different question. DERIVED, checked by independent quadrature (70 quadratures in the orbital folder, and a separate integration that reproduces every digit above).

The sudden-change overlap itself is established atomic physics — it is the same formula used for an electron staying bound when a nucleus changes charge in beta decay. What is new is that its scale coordinate is my face apex. In this derivation zz compares two one-electron Hamiltonians; carrying it to two successive measured removals in one many-electron atom needs the initial state, the final projector and the physical change specified. That is a structural link, not yet a measurement.

A three-state loop of orbital projectors at scales 1, 2 and 4 carries a sign: its three-state trace is negative for 2s and positive for 2p. The orbital label, not only the energy ratio, decides the turn of the loop. DERIVED (Coulomb loop folder).

Hypothesis and its control. I assign clocks to the layers inside an atom and compare the facing clocks of its neighbours. Swapping them changes the experiment. At a matched junction z=1z = 1 and Γ=0\Gamma = 0 even when the internal ladder is steep. For sodium’s L opening, the weakest projector link changes from about 0.000292 to 0.000865 when the opening moves from the facing link into the cell. For argon’s first ordinary step the change is about 0.000804 to 0.000874. The difference between these two outputs drops by about 98 percent, and both stay below 1/121/12. Both runs use two-level hydrogen cells. The result isolates the effect of assigning clocks to different links; it supplies no conductivity for either element.

Six experiments that give “wall”, “gap” and “tree” different jobs

1. Balls in the sea. The research folder implements three choices of state preparation and dynamics. Model A builds a global Hamiltonian with site and link terms. Model B starts with occupied cells and empty links. Model C releases a disturbance from an occupied resting state with finite travel on the connections. The 396 recorded executions span 100 settings, or “ways”. A successful execution only says the program returned. A representative sealed A run conserves its ledger and yet responds across the model too early for the proposed transit rule. C can pass the transit test while missing the prescribed threshold for an initial non-local block. Preparing a correlated ground state and sending a new disturbance through it ask different questions. Changing a numerical detection threshold changes what counts as a first arrival in a continuous-time lattice. The squeeze test modulates a clock sinusoidally; associating its stored energy with a thermodynamic temperature needs an independently specified ensemble or thermometer.

2. Hydrogen in the space between. Each centre has six facing ports. Gap sites carry hoppings c=c0sech(12logz)c = c_0\,\mathrm{sech}\big(\tfrac12\log z\big). Let PP be the occupied one-particle projector and Ci=PiiC_i = P_{ii} its restriction to a cell. The iiii block of P2=PP^2 = P gives Ci2+∑j≠iPijPji=Ci,∑j≠i∥Pij∥F2=Tr(Ci−Ci2).C_i^2 + \sum_{j\ne i}P_{ij}P_{ji} = C_i,\qquad \sum_{j\ne i}\|P_{ij}\|_F^2 = \operatorname{Tr}\big(C_i - C_i^2\big). The trace is the available correlation weight; the individual squared block norms say where that weight goes. A two-centre, separation-four, half-filled example has 75 sites and 150 one-particle coordinates. Its weakest path link is about 6.416×10−46.416\times10^{-4} against the study’s 1/121/12 marker. The opposed setting has lower energy than the parallel setting by about 0.09968 model energy units at this fixed separation. Other separations change the number of sites, so total energies there need a common reference before a binding curve can be inferred. Threshold first arrivals in the recorded sweep occur at 0.7, 3.9 and 8.1 model time units at separations two, four and six. Test: hold the Hilbert space, filling and energy reference fixed and compare the force inferred from the separation derivative; freeze the detector threshold before the travel test and publish the threshold dependence.

3. Hydrogen and the light between. Timing enters explicitly here. In the recorded aligned and detuned runs the first detection at C moves from 5.37 to 8.67, while the light at C moves from 0.0250 to 0.0161. Those values depend on a detector and an update rule. One original regression criterion asked the zero-coupling model to reproduce v4 to 10−1210^{-12}; a later comparison records a discrepancy of 0.0743 at B and withdraws that criterion because the face positions differ. Both the discrepancy and its reason belong in the record. Test: match the geometries and input pulse before attributing any residual to a new propagation law.

4. Seven balls, my light. A central cell and six neighbours separate the intrinsic wall-ray experiment from light propagated through the room. The intrinsic rule keeps a ray near radius 0.985 in a representative run; the room rule can carry light into other balls. One finite trace accounts for 12 units emitted as about 2.6635 in flight, 9.3364 in the ground and 0.0001 below the cut. These are entries in a code ledger. The proposed links to optical transmission, absorption and heating each need a map from such entries to an instrument.

5. The ball is the tree. The 37-cell construction has thirty leaves. Comparing paths by summed intrinsic edge length gives two layers of total length 2log32\log3 in the example. The arrival test respects the layer delay, and a leaf’s ground does not transmit onward under the specified rule. The proposed equality of a pair of twins fails its initial tolerance, with a difference near 7×10−57\times10^{-5}. Refining the time step from 0.04 to 0.005 reduces another twin comparison from 4.70×10−44.70\times10^{-4} to 2.38×10−52.38\times10^{-5}; a convergence trend leaves the exact equality open. The model gives an operational meaning to my phrase “it just knows layers”. Equal total layer depth need not mean equal local environments, sources or path histories.

6. Two atoms in a ball. The container adds a separate wall-work term. Across eight settings, the total of energy in cells and stretches plus outgoing energy, less supplied wall work, differs from the unit input by at most about 1.6×10−141.6\times10^{-14}. A single moving-mirror control with reflectivity amplitude ρ=1/2\rho = 1/2 and dimensionless speed v=0.2v = 0.2 has reflected energy ρ2(1+v)/(1−v)=0.375\rho^2(1+v)/(1-v) = 0.375 and supplied work 0.125. The strict zero-outside control for a closed container misses zero by about 7.884×10−57.884\times10^{-5} in one run and 2.59×10−52.59\times10^{-5} after refinement. Conservation and confinement are independent tests, and treating the small residual as exactly zero would erase one of them.

What a projector link can read

DERIVED with conditions. Put Bi=Tr(Ci−Ci2)B_i = \operatorname{Tr}(C_i - C_i^2) and specify nn equivalent candidate neighbours. The proposed link marker is Xij>Bi/(3n)X_{ij} > B_i/(3n). One half-filled mode gives Bi=1/4B_i = 1/4; two equivalent neighbours would give 1/241/24, and four give 1/481/48. A number reported for a particular lattice also depends on the chosen mode count, coordination and projector. The unnormalised 1/121/12 arises as (1/4)/3(1/4)/3. The sum rule licenses an allocation of weight; the factor of three and the choice of neighbour shell need their own model assumptions. In the follow-up runs a half-filled bcc band passes, sufficiently dilute fillings fail (the proved sufficient bound is f≤1/25f\le1/25), and a filled gapped band passes. The gapped positive is decisive for interpretation: the criterion can select concentrated intercell weights in an insulator. A conductivity claim needs a current operator, a response protocol, and a thermodynamic or stated finite-size limit. The Bruggeman one-third marker belongs to a separately specified effective-medium comparison. A chemical element carries no universal “above one third” label independent of phase and observable.

The same sum rule is already known in quantum chemistry: the sum of delocalisation indices of an atom over its partners equals its own fluctuation, and the localisation tensor is the second moment of the same weights. My junction budget and that identity are one fact, read on my projector. DERIVED.

Two unequal faces, one exact wall

For the specified two-boost commutator the trace is 2−4sinh2(ha)sinh2(hb)2 - 4\sinh^2(h_a)\sinh^2(h_b), where hi=12logzih_i = \tfrac12\log z_i. At trace −2-2 the product of the squared hyperbolic sines is one. With u=Γa2u = \Gamma_a^2, v=Γb2v = \Gamma_b^2 and u,v<1u, v<1, the condition uv=(1−u)(1−v)uv = (1-u)(1-v) reduces exactly to u+v=1u+v = 1. Ordinary forward steps allow positive square roots; keeping the squares keeps both reverse branches. Equal faces give u=v=1/2u = v = 1/2. At the boundary the usual Jordan test decides whether a matrix of trace −2-2 is a non-trivial parabolic block or the scalar −I-I.

In my convention carbon’s helium-core opening is on the open side with both faces the same, and nitrogen’s is on the closed side with both faces the same. The mixed pair — carbon’s helium-core opening ratio paired with nitrogen’s — is barely open: Γa2+Γb2−1=+0.00309\Gamma_a^2 + \Gamma_b^2 - 1 = +0.00309. Among the 427 adjacent same-core pairs of first openings, it is the pair nearest ideal contact: 5 pairs open and 422 close, and this pair’s margin is below 0.0031 against rivals above 0.037. Holding carbon at 392.09056/64.49352=6.079534392.09056/64.49352 = 6.079534, the partner’s forward ratio for exact contact is 5.5911565.591156. The five open pairs are lithium with beryllium, beryllium with boron, boron with carbon, carbon with nitrogen and sodium with magnesium, all helium-core or neon-core first openings. In the angle form, with θ=arcsinΓ\theta = \arcsin\Gamma, the loop test is θa+θb<90∘\theta_a + \theta_b < 90^\circ; the boundary pair of each core — the last element outside paired with the first inside — reads carbon with nitrogen +0.18∘+0.18^\circ (open), sodium with magnesium +6.67∘+6.67^\circ (open), potassium with calcium −2.21∘-2.21^\circ, rubidium with strontium −6.52∘-6.52^\circ and caesium with barium −10.29∘-10.29^\circ (all close). Allowing the two faces to meet at an angle other than a right angle, the carbon–nitrogen loop closes only for meeting angles between 13.115∘13.115^\circ and 89.823∘89.823^\circ. These claims concern the selected commutator with clocks read from two removal energies. Demonstrating a physical closed path would need an independently measured return observable. The unequal-face test is more informative than labelling two elements, because fixing one face predicts quantitatively where the partner crosses.

My other papers read at the wall

The wall did not arrive alone. Each of my earlier papers has its own objects, and when I write them in the variables of one peel step the same number appears. I separate three grades here: EXACT means the same formula by algebra; STRUCTURAL means the same shape on different objects; LEAD means untested or tested only in part.

The Offset Belongs to the Boundary

For an eigenvalue 0<ν<10<\nu<1 of a specified restricted correlation operator, define z=(1−ν)/νz = (1-\nu)/\nu. Then Γ=1−2ν,ν(1−ν)=1−Γ24,S=41−Γ2.\Gamma = 1-2\nu,\qquad \nu(1-\nu) = \frac{1-\Gamma^2}{4},\qquad S = \frac{4}{1-\Gamma^2}. Every entanglement level is a peel step, and the per-mode offset τν=ln((1−ν)/ν)\tau_\nu = \ln\big((1-\nu)/\nu\big) is the peel rapidity lnz\ln z. The equal-face wall gives census ν(1−ν)=1/8\nu(1-\nu) = 1/8 — exactly half of the half-filling maximum 1/41/4 — and sharpness S=8S = 8; the per-mode offset there is ln(3+22)=2arsinh1\ln(3+2\sqrt2) = 2\operatorname{arsinh}1. The census window |τ|≤ln(3+22)|\tau|\le\ln(3+2\sqrt2) is the same statement as ν(1−ν)≥1/8\nu(1-\nu)\ge1/8. EXACT.

On the archive, S>8S > 8 gives the same call as z>3+22z > 3+2\sqrt2 on every one of the 3,570 ordinary steps from hydrogen to astatine, and on all 44 bound anions from hydrogen to caesium, with no disagreement. At the anion rung S0=(IE+EA)2/(IE⋅EA)=4/(1−Γ02)S_0 = (IE+EA)^2/(IE\cdot EA) = 4/(1-\Gamma_0^2), so S0=8S_0 = 8 is exactly electrophilicity equal to hardness; silver has S0=7.9801S_0 = 7.9801 (inside) and silicon 8.03708.0370 (outside). EXACT, checked.

Putting two atomic threshold energies into ν=IEk/(IEk+IEk+1)\nu = IE_k/(IE_k+IE_{k+1}) is an exact numerical encoding. Identifying that number with the correlation eigenvalue of an independently prepared state is a further physical hypothesis. In the Rice–Mele comparison, positive hoppings t1t_1, t2t_2 and staggering vv give a squared band-edge ratio of one half exactly at t12+t22+v2=6t1t2t_1^2+t_2^2+v^2 = 6t_1t_2; at v=0v = 0, t2/t1=3±22t_2/t_1 = 3\pm2\sqrt2. The offset ladder spacing becomes 4π4\pi exactly at the wall, and the offset reaches ln(3+22)\ln(3+2\sqrt2) at v=2t/3v = 2t/\sqrt3. Finite-block calculations at interior sample points carry a different evidential status from an all-parameter proof. The v31 edition identifies the log-determinant ratio with the empty-region to full-region probability ratio for a number-conserving Gaussian state with 0<CA<I0<C_A<I. Its large odd-block Rice–Mele result takes a fixed connected gapped model; a dimensional cosmological constant would need a calibration and a variational or selection principle.

What Transport Keeps

Iterating a real determinant-one matrix with distinct real eigenvalues of different moduli selects the expanding projective direction from a generic starting line. A defective parabolic block selects algebraically; an elliptic block can rotate without selecting any real line. So the trace wall trW=−2\operatorname{tr}W = -2 is exactly where line selection switches on in this family, subject to initial-vector and degeneracy conditions. In the specified corner frame the interior projector conditioning obeys κ2=1/(1−Γa2−Γb2)\kappa^2 = 1/(1-\Gamma_a^2-\Gamma_b^2), and Proposition 7’s rank-one stress is S=Γa2+Γb2S = \Gamma_a^2+\Gamma_b^2. The divergence near the wall depends on the metric used for norms and on the chosen frame: similarity preserves the eigenvalue classification while a non-unitary change of basis can alter a projector norm, which stops a conditioning plot from becoming a claimed intrinsic material observable. EXACT for the algebra.

The rail coordinate makes the wall and Catalan’s constant one coordinate. Put Γ=tan(ψ/2)\Gamma = \tan(\psi/2). The wall Γ2=12\Gamma^2 = \tfrac12 sits at cosψ=1/3\cos\psi = 1/3, that is secψ=3\sec\psi = 3. Catalan’s rail root 17+122=(3+22)217+12\sqrt2 = (3+2\sqrt2)^2 has reflection 22/3=tanh(2h*)2\sqrt2/3 = \tanh(2h_*), where h*=arsinh1h_* = \operatorname{arsinh}1 is the wall half-step: the Catalan rail’s rapidity is exactly twice the wall’s. And G=∫012artanhΓ1+Γ2dΓ=0.9159655941772190…,G = \int_0^1 \frac{2\operatorname{artanh}\Gamma}{1+\Gamma^2}\,d\Gamma = 0.9159655941772190\ldots, equal to Catalan’s constant at 45 digits — the peel half-step weighted by dψ/dΓd\psi/d\Gamma. This is a direct change of variable of a classical integral; I claim no physical meaning for Catalan’s constant from it. EXACT. Edition 3 also gives a normalised-Gram test for selection of a dominant right singular projector: tied growth can give a fixed line, a rotating line or an unresolved higher-dimensional block, and discrete plaquette compatibility of its transport and curvature of its eigenline refer to different connections and can coexist.

The Offset Speed Limit — rate is weight

A differentiable path of projectors supplies a clock that a list of ionisations lacks. With g=12∥Ṗ∥F2g = \tfrac12\|\dot P\|_F^2 and, for Ṗ=−i[H,P]\dot P = -i[H,P] with ℏ=1\hbar=1, g=∥PH(I−P)∥F2=EBg = \|PH(I-P)\|_F^2 = E_B, the speed limit reads τ̇2≤4gS\dot\tau^2\le 4gS. The Weight Between

On one scalar edge carrying two thresholds, the matrix definitions of The Weight Between give the two books directly: E−=18∥[H,H†]∥2=(di−dj)2E^- = \tfrac18\|[H,H^\dagger]\|^2 = (d_i-d_j)^2 and E+=18∥H2−H†2∥2=(di+dj)2E^+ = \tfrac18\|H^2-H^{\dagger2}\|^2 = (d_i+d_j)^2, so E−/E+=Γ2E^-/E^+ = \Gamma^2 and (E+−E−)/E+=4ν(1−ν)(E^+-E^-)/E^+ = 4\nu(1-\nu), the census. The Ledger Outlives the Metric

In the gravity ledger the local positivity calculation uses a Hermitian form with diagonal entries aa, cc and upper off-diagonal b+iω/2b + i\omega/2. Positivity needs a,c≥0a,c\ge0 and 4(ac−b2)≥ω24(ac-b^2)\ge\omega^2. In the normalisation a=c=1a = c = 1, b=Γab = \Gamma_a, ω=2Γb\omega = 2\Gamma_b, its boundary is again Γa2+Γb2=1\Gamma_a^2+\Gamma_b^2 = 1: the two-face rule is the rank-one licence of that paper. This is a reversible translation between the clock disc and a positivity domain for that particular form. It does not specify a mass distribution, a rotation curve, a physical spacetime metric or a source for gravitation; a gravitational reading would need predictions in its own measured variables and a map into this disc fixed before fitting them. The final edition defines its intrinsic real trace form explicitly as gij=12ReTr(∂iP∂jP)g_{ij} = \tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(\partial_iP\,\partial_jP). A rank-one Riesz projector can cross a positivity wall while its contour stays gapped and the selected trace log varies smoothly. The paper’s spectral-screen grid comparison has a largest sampled negative residual of about −0.07954-0.07954 dex against a comparison curve; it is not a fit to individual galaxy points. A source Hessian gives a susceptibility; a force law also needs an energy, a physical Green function and a source calibration.

In the element work’s own hyperboloid form of this licence, the anion rung has metric determinant detg=IE×EA\det g = IE\times EA, and the wall is a sign change of a two-plane Gram determinant; these are constructions of the element paper, not statements of the gravity ledger’s trace form. Reversing an nn-step path multiplies its signed volume by (−1)n(n+1)/2(-1)^{n(n+1)/2}. EXACT for the algebra.

Matter at a Scale

Difference observables are invariant under K↦K+cIK\mapsto K+cI and projectors are invariant under K↦cKK\mapsto cK. Each removal energy is a difference of charge-state energies, so a common shift of every charge-state energy cancels in it, and a common scale cancels in the ratio: Γ\Gamma does not change when every ionisation energy is scaled together. It does change if every ionisation energy is shifted by one constant — adding 5 eV to every removal energy moves carbon’s fourth step from Γ2=0.5148\Gamma^2 = 0.5148 to 0.4930, across the wall. That is why one threshold can be laid across all the elements, and why an absolute anchor — a mass, a clock — is needed the moment a prediction is stated in units. EXACT. The scale paper’s anomaly coefficient A=2c/π2A = 2c/\pi^2 (per two endpoints) belongs to the logarithm between zero and span; whether the wall’s logarithm ln(3+22)\ln(3+2\sqrt2) has a place in that census is LEAD.

The Offset Speed Limit, What Transport Keeps and the companion editions: scope

The Offset Speed Limit v1.1 starts from a differentiable family of finite orthogonal projectors; its proof uses orthogonal projectors throughout. What Transport Keeps edition 3 keeps its own transport and curvature connections apart. These scope conditions travel with every use above.

The element test from hydrogen to astatine

The atom is the first place in this programme where the ordered object can be specified without a geometric drawing. Removing the electron from the negative ion and ionising the neutral atom are different experiments; their energy ratio supplies the extra zeroth rung, the anion rung. The 3,655 positive-index energies are 290 experimental, 847 semiempirical and 2,518 theoretical entries in the archive’s grade system; an energy’s grade does not fix the leading configuration of either state. Where a rectangle crosses z=1z = 1 the minimum squared reflection is zero. The width calculation expresses sensitivity to assumptions on the inputs: quoted error bars provide neither simultaneous confidence nor a known joint correlation model.

Three boundaries in every element

I read each element at its anion rung (z0=IE1/EAz_0 = IE_1/EA, where a bound anion exists) and at each closed-core opening: the last removal above the core, then the first removal from it.

  • K opening — the opening of the helium-like 1s21s^2 core (2s→1s2s\to1s).
  • L opening — the opening of the neon-like core (3s→2p3s\to2p).
  • Argon-core opening (the M opening) — 4s→3p4s\to3p for potassium and calcium, and from scandium onward the last 3d3d removal to 3p3p. That last kind keeps the principal shell (both are n=3n = 3), so its bare hydrogenic ratio is 1, not 16/916/9.
  • Krypton-core opening — the 4s24p64s^24p^6 core, from rubidium on.
  • Xenon-core opening — the 5s25p65s^25p^6 core, from caesium on.

The full 85-row table of these six boundaries, each cell with zz and Γ\Gamma, is in the appendix The element table. Reading it down the columns (RECOGNISED):

  • K opening: outside from lithium to carbon, crosses inward between carbon (6.08) and nitrogen (5.64), and stays inside from then on.
  • L opening: outside only at sodium (9.20).
  • Argon-core opening: outside only at potassium (7.29).
  • Krypton-core opening: outside only at rubidium (6.53).
  • Xenon-core opening: outside only at caesium (5.95), the smallest outside ordinary value in the catalogue.

The eight ordinary outside steps from hydrogen to astatine — none new after caesium — are all first core openings: lithium, beryllium, boron and carbon at the helium core, and sodium, potassium, rubidium and caesium at the neon, argon, krypton and xenon cores. A change of shell alone always lands inside: the bare hydrogenic floors 4,9/4,16/9,25/16,36/25,49/364, 9/4, 16/9, 25/16, 36/25, 49/36 are all inside. An opening can stand outside only through a departure from the bare shell, which screening provides at low ZZ, and that departure shrinks shell by shell.

Anion rung: outside for most bound anions, but inside for fluorine, sulfur, chlorine, selenium, bromine, silver, tellurium, iodine, iridium, platinum, gold and astatine — the strong electron attachers. Across gallium to bromine it runs outside, outside, outside, inside, inside; arsenic stands above germanium because its first removal energy is higher and its affinity lower at the same time. Two elements make the boundaries visible. Oxygen stands on both sides at once: its anion rung is outside and its core opening inside (Lean: oxygen_two_sides). Silver and silicon are the closest calls: silver’s anion rung sits just inside (Γ0=0.70622\Gamma_0 = 0.70622) and silicon’s just outside (Γ0=0.70873\Gamma_0 = 0.70873), against the wall at 0.70711, each on its side across its quoted uncertainties (Lean: rung0_Si_low, rung0_Si_high). Neon’s helium-core ratio is strictly greater than five, just above Γ=2/3\Gamma = 2/3.

Conduction does not need an outside step. Magnesium and calcium are metals with every ordinary step inside (Lean: mg_all_inside, ca_all_ordinary_inside), and so are scandium to zinc, gallium, strontium, yttrium to silver, indium and tin. The wall reads the atom’s own ladder. Conduction is a property of the connections between atoms, and I take it up with the junctions. Conductivity or not is still, to me, the key in every element — set by the electron, with light as its twin guiding it — and the record of that is in the junction section, not in the single-atom ladder.

The strongest ordinary step changes rank in the third and fourth periods: from the L opening to the K opening between magnesium and aluminium, and from the argon-core opening to the K opening between potassium and calcium (Lean: rank_swap_Mg_Al, rank_swap_K_Ca). The filled 3d103d^{10} and 4d104d^{10} openings decline across their rows; palladium’s anion rung is its own filled 4d104d^{10} opening, and no filled 4d104d^{10} ordinary opening exists from niobium to rhodium.

The jump as a loop: closing and opening

DERIVED. The wall can be read without the sinh formula. Put the corner of a ball at the centre of the disc, with one face along each of two perpendicular directions. Each face sits at its half-step distance h=12lnzh = \tfrac12\ln z from the corner. At each face draw the line perpendicular to its direction; in the disc that line is a circle meeting the rim at right angles, with radius 1/sinhh1/\sinh h. The two circles cross exactly when sinhhasinhhb<1\sinh h_a\sinh h_b<1. When they cross, the loop around the step closes; when they miss, it is open. The border case is the classical quadrilateral with three right angles and its fourth corner on the rim — the Lambert quadrilateral. For equal faces the border is z=3+22z = 3+2\sqrt2, the loop wall. Closed, cosϕ=sinhasinhb\cos\phi = \sinh a\sinh b; open, coshd=sinhasinhb\cosh d = \sinh a\sinh b. Across all 5,714 central ratios, no ratio separates the geometric wall from the registered arithmetic-midpoint rival; of the 5,691 pairs with both widths recorded, one interval overlaps the test window (francium), and 23 lack a complete width. The geometry selects an exact number before any fit; the census gives a range with identical classifications. So the data cannot by themselves pick 3+223+2\sqrt2 out of the window, and the uniqueness has to come from the geometry — which is exactly what the two-face agreement theorem supplies. A physical test that could tell the wall from its neighbours would need an independently measured observable that changes characteristically across the window, with its threshold and error budget fixed in advance. The carbon and nitrogen K-resonance areas show why such an observable is needed: their reported areas overlap within quoted uncertainties, so they do not separate the two sides.

RECOGNISED. The inside set is not the metals against the non-metals, not the metalloid line, and not hard against soft. Silver (ω/η=1.0025\omega/\eta = 1.0025) and silicon (0.99540.9954) bracket the wall. The quantities η\eta, χ\chi and ω\omega are standard (Parr and Pearson 1983; Parr, von Szentpály and Liu 1999), but I found no published use of ω=η\omega = \eta, η/χ=1/2\eta/\chi = 1/\sqrt2 or IE/EA=3+22IE/EA = 3+2\sqrt2 as a boundary. The full 65-row table of IE/EAIE/EA, η/χ\eta/\chi and ω/η\omega/\eta is in the appendix. Calcium, strontium and barium do bind an extra electron (affinities 0.02455, 0.05206 and 0.14462 eV): their anion rungs are far outside, at 249.0, 109.4 and 36.0. Among the alkaline earths through barium, only beryllium and magnesium have no stable anion.

PREDICTION TESTED. Written at 09:24 on 21 November 2026, before the adopted values were opened, as informed calls from remembered chemistry (correlated with one another, not independent tests): gold, platinum, iridium and astatine inside, with iridium close to the wall; osmium, bismuth, polonium and lead outside. Result: gold 3.996, platinum 4.216, iridium 5.733 and astatine 3.857 are inside; osmium 7.830, bismuth 7.731 and lead 20.79 are outside. All seven cases with adopted experimental point values agree (Lean: heavy_anion_prediction). The eighth call, polonium outside, failed this way, provisionally: three preliminary laser photodetachment fits from one campaign put it inside — the JyvIS value 11,905.631(9)cm−111{,}905.631(9)\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}} gives A=1.4761101164A = 1.4761101164 eV and z=5.702874z = 5.702874 — and the wall would need A<1.444312474A<1.444312474 eV for outside. The team explicitly excludes unfinalised systematics from the reported uncertainty, and the fits are not independent experiments. With the same provisional affinity the barium-donor, polonium-acceptor pair gives about 5.2117/1.476110=3.5315.2117/1.476110 = 3.531, also inside. Gold and platinum are known to form monatomic anions in real compounds. These seven heavy calls do not, by themselves, single out 3+223+2\sqrt2 among cutoffs between 5.8 and 6. A separate holdout rule that predicted anion side from the ordinary call and the position of the strongest opening, trained on hydrogen to xenon, called every caesium-to-astatine case outside: 20 of 20 outside correct, 0 of 4 inside, balanced accuracy 0.50, missing iridium, platinum, gold and astatine. That rule failed this way. The strongest opening still gives a useful address: it occurs deeper than the first eligible core for 70 of 83 elements, and adding its ordinal to the anion and ordinary address reduces the number of indistinguishable element pairs from 1,304 to 366.

The element address

Each element’s address is where its two strongest boundaries fall: the anion rung (inside, outside or none) and the first opening of its noble-gas core (inside, outside or none). From hydrogen to astatine this gives seven occupied classes:

Anion rung First core opening Elements Count
outside outside lithium, boron, carbon, sodium, potassium, rubidium, caesium 7
none outside beryllium 1
outside inside 45 elements, including oxygen, aluminium, silicon, phosphorus, calcium, strontium, barium and most transition metals 45
inside inside fluorine, sulfur, chlorine, selenium, bromine, silver, tellurium, iodine, iridium, platinum, gold, astatine 12
none inside 18 elements, including the noble gases from neon on, magnesium, nitrogen, zinc, mercury 18
outside none hydrogen 1
none none helium 1

DERIVED from measured inputs. The out-and-out class — lithium, boron, carbon, sodium, potassium, rubidium and caesium — is the set of atoms where both the extra electron and the first core electron are held past the wall. This address is the backbone of my Periodic Table of Elemental Peels.

The gold–mercury bracket

DERIVED / HOLDOUT. The one-electron shell ratio 4 plays two roles. In the unscreened Schrödinger (scalar-wave) 2s→1s2s\to1s comparison it gives Γ=3/5\Gamma = 3/5. The actual lithium-like to helium-like pair includes state-dependent electronic binding and follows a different sequence. All 82 consecutive uncertainty-box comparisons from lithium to astatine descend strictly. The ratio first falls below four between gold, 4.00189784, and mercury, 3.99780412; both heavy inputs in each pair are theory-grade. A straight secant based on terbium and ytterbium, and a point-Coulomb Dirac ratio with a fitted 1/Z1/Z correction, both predicted this bracket from truncated inputs (intervals [4.001832223,4.001963460][4.001832223, 4.001963460] and [3.997740439,3.997867804][3.997740439, 3.997867804]). Only two of 15 held-out point predictions for the secant enter the tabulated intervals, and zero of 15 for the corrected spinor formula.
