A preregistered successful bracket can coexist with a poor pointwise error model, and gold–mercury shows both.

A transfer that failed this way

DERIVED / FAILED TRANSFER. For four log-steps rir_i spanning a core, divide each by ∑iri\sum_ir_i. The resulting shape says where an endpoint-fixed ratio accumulates. The frozen first-two contrast gave 72 of 72 positions in the lighter neon-, argon- and krypton-count families. On the 24 xenon-count positions it gave 14 of 24; the ordered four-component classifier gave 15 of 24. Eleven primary responses remain correct and three remain wrong across complete input boxes; ten are ambiguous within those boxes. In Ce²⁺ the primary contrast is positive, about 0.018854, while the required class lies below −0.163945-0.163945. A ratio can be reliably measured and still be a poor predictor of a transferred label. The subshell bookkeeping supplies an independent control: across the 605 removals from barium to terbium it counts 595 with zero required reassignment, nine with one, and one gadolinium step with two, under the ASD leading configurations; an alternative sequence of configurations removes the apparent gadolinium 1, 2, 1 episode. Writing occupations aℓa_\ell before a peel and bℓb_\ell after it, K=∑min(aℓ,bℓ)K = \sum\min(a_\ell,b_\ell) counts slots matchable within each subshell and R=∑(bℓ−aℓ)+R = \sum(b_\ell-a_\ell)_+ counts the remaining target slots; Nafter=K+RN_{\text{after}} = K+R and ∥a−b∥1=2R+1\|a-b\|_1 = 2R+1 for a one-particle loss. None identifies an individual electron.

Three physical checks on what an elemental ladder keeps

DERIVED / MEASURED INPUTS. Electron removal leaves the proton and neutron counts of a chosen isotope unchanged; nuclear transmutation is a second process. For two isobars at equal ionic charge the missing-electron rest energies cancel. Defining Q(q)=[MHo(q)−MDy(q)]c2Q(q) = [M_{\mathrm{Ho}}(q)-M_{\mathrm{Dy}}(q)]c^2 gives ΔQ=IHo,q+1−IDy,q+1\Delta Q = I_{\mathrm{Ho},q+1}-I_{\mathrm{Dy},q+1}, which is (IHo+IDy)ΓHo,Dy(I_{\mathrm{Ho}}+I_{\mathrm{Dy}})\,\Gamma_{\mathrm{Ho,Dy}} with the signed interspecies reflection taken at equal charge. Observed neutral holmium-163 decays toward dysprosium; bare dysprosium-163 was observed to decay the other way, to hydrogen-like holmium. The independent neutral mass anchor and the archive predict only one ground-mass-ordering reversal, from Q(56)=+1.9514Q(56) = +1.9514 keV to Q(57)=−4.5186Q(57) = -4.5186 keV. Separate restarts from the published 38+, 39+ and 40+ trap frequency ratios keep the bracket. At 56+ the two species have eleven and ten electrons, so the next removal opens dysprosium’s neon-like core while holmium still loses its last 3s3s electron, which drives a −6.470-6.470 keV increment. No intermediate-charge decay rate was measured. Multiplying both energy ladders by 0.01 while holding neutral Q(0)Q(0) fixed erases the ordering change and keeps every adjacent and interspecies reflection — an explicit identifiability control on a dimensionless-only model. The full calculation is in Where the vector reaches nuclear decay.

DERIVED / CONTROL. In the lead-205 and thallium-205 system the signed mass gap crosses between 79+ and 80+. Subtracting the 2.329 keV daughter nuclear excitation from the bare-endpoint calculation gives 31.0715 keV for the dominant bound-electron channel; the published 31.1(5) keV shares the neutral mass baseline, and the directly observed stored-ion decay is independent evidence that the channel opens. Rhenium gives a different control: the same elemental electronic ladder applied to rhenium-185 and rhenium-187 gives opposite outcomes because of their different nuclear mass anchors. For rhenium-187 a directly measured rhenium–osmium 29+ mass difference removes the need to accumulate both sets of outer-shell uncertainties; the bare parent then has about 63.005 keV available to the osmium-187 excited state at 9.756 keV via the daughter K shell, while the neutral endpoint falls short by about 7.285 keV. The proposed 2s2s channel to that excited state straddles zero within the stated interval, so its status stays open.

MEASURED INPUT / RECOGNISED. Structure and photons can change independently of any free-atom peel ratio. The two crystallographic sites of double-hcp neodymium agree in their first twelve distances and second moments yet differ in their angular environment. In coexisting ytterbium refinements some shortest contacts lengthen as the molar volume falls. For elemental polonium the alpha-to-beta refinements give six closest neighbours in both cases, with the shortest distance increasing while the volume per atom declines. Osmium gives direction-resolved optics in one crystal: at 650 nm the two principal-polarisation reflectances from the measured complex indices are 0.4846 and 0.5285. Both belong to the same isotope-averaged electronic ladder. For astatine-197 one nuclear-state change at fixed ZZ, NN shifts the 216 nm line up by 4,215 MHz and the 795 nm line down by 1,868 MHz. These examples ask the theory to say which distance, state, direction and optical transition it aims to predict. Neither a signed crystal path nor a nuclear-state label supplies an atomic HOMFLY or Jones invariant without a chosen embedding and closure.

Reproducibility and retained discrepancies

All 3,655 positive-index energy cells in the corrected historical tables match the pinned archive exactly. I rebuilt 3,740 indexed rows (3,655 removal energies plus 85 anion slots). The early magnesium k=4k = 4 table displays 0.12800 for Γ\Gamma, which recomputes as 0.127953665550. The scandium affinity display 0.179380 eV differs from the adopted 0.179378 eV, so the zero-rung ratio is 36.579123. Selenium has a conversion-rounding discrepancy below 10−2710^{-27} eV. Every typed energy in the seventeen batch tables was compared with the archive; the corrections — vanadium k=11k = 11, chromium k=9k = 9 and k=20k = 20, nickel k=21k = 21, copper k=5k = 5 and the magnesium k=4k = 4 display — change no wall classification. In the independent 21 November ASD snapshot for barium to astatine, 2,114 of 2,115 records agree in value, uncertainty, grade and references with the older pin; neutral neodymium changed from 5.5250(6) to 5.52475(5) eV. The repository folder carries the full threshold table, a one-row-per-element index, the field-level discrepancy file and a standalone reconstruction script.

Colour and the half-power line

This section uses Elizabeth Johnson’s Mixin colour system, credited by name; the algebra that maps it onto the peel is mine and is marked.

The colour line

The complex optical coordinate of my Volume paper is (1−N)/(1+N)(1-N)/(1+N), where N=n+iκN = n+i\kappa is the complex refractive index: the same Smith form as the peel, with the index in place of the clock ratio. At normal incidence from vacuum on a homogeneous non-magnetic half-space its squared modulus is the reflectance, R=|Γopt|2=(n−1)2+κ2(n+1)2+κ2,R = |\Gamma_{\text{opt}}|^2 = \frac{(n-1)^2+\kappa^2}{(n+1)^2+\kappa^2}, and R−12R-\tfrac12 has the sign of (n−3)2+κ2−8(n-3)^2+\kappa^2-8 (Lean: circle_identity in OpticalWall.lean). The half-power circle |Γ|2=12|\Gamma|^2 = \tfrac12 is the same circle as the loop wall on my Smith disc.

MEASURED INPUTS, DERIVED CALL. Averaged over the visible band, all 35 metals with optical data reflect above |Γ|2=12|\Gamma|^2 = \tfrac12, and none of the 6 non-metals do. Niobium is the closest metal (0.5026) and tellurium the closest non-metal (0.4940). The data are the refractive-index sets used in my vacuum-disk paper (v6). The source also reports that phase gaps predict thin-film colour differences among 39 pairs similar in bulk, with rank correlation 0.64, and in a finite-film closure test a frozen reflection threshold |Γ|=0.856|\Gamma| = 0.856 scored 87% on 171 film cases. The same number one half appears for the isolated atom’s ladder and for the bulk metal’s mirror, but they are different inputs and different detectors; the colour line is a classification of metals by their optical response, not a consequence of the atomic peel. The osmium control makes this concrete: at 650 nm the two principal polarisations of one osmium crystal give 0.48460 and 0.52845, straddling the half-power line while the isolated-atom ladder is unchanged.

Mixin and the wall circle

In my polarisation encoding of Elizabeth’s Mixin labels (the mixin-colors repository), the secondary colours come out at a degree of polarisation 1/21/\sqrt2. That is a circle of radius 1/21/\sqrt2 on the polarisation sphere — a different disc from my Smith disc, so this is a match of numbers, not of objects. Whether colour perception reads that circle as a boundary is OPEN.

The ledger and the colour balance

The non-Riemannian geometry in my work belongs to the ledger comparison. In Foundational Operator Field Theory v2 (§13.3) an observer compares two interface states through the trace-log ledger, S(A,B)=logdetA+B2−12logdetA−12logdetBS(A,B) = \log\det\frac{A+B}{2} - \tfrac12\log\det A - \tfrac12\log\det B. Close up, S\sqrt S is a fixed multiple of the Riemannian transport metric, dS/dδR→1/(22)d\sqrt S/d\delta_R \to 1/(2\sqrt2); over large jumps it falls short of the sum of its small steps. Locally Riemannian, globally subadditive: diminishing returns are the shape of this geometry.

For two intensities II and JJ the ledger has a closed form in my peel coordinate. With Γ=(I−J)/(I+J)=tanh(12ln(I/J))\Gamma = (I-J)/(I+J) = \tanh(\tfrac12\ln(I/J)),

S(I,J)=logcosh(12lnIJ)=−12ln(1−Γ2),S(I,J) = \log\cosh\left(\tfrac12\ln\frac IJ\right) = -\tfrac12\ln(1-\Gamma^2),

so the ledger between two neighbouring peel thresholds is a function of their Γ\Gamma alone, and at the wall Γ2=12\Gamma^2 = \tfrac12 it is exactly 12ln2\tfrac12\ln2. Its derivative is the balance map of Colour Selects the Leader (v1.2, §§8 and 12): ddxlogcosh(x/2)=12tanh(x/2)\tfrac{d}{dx}\log\cosh(x/2) = \tfrac12\tanh(x/2), the Smith reflection (z−1)/(z+1)(z-1)/(z+1). The square root S\sqrt S is a distance (S. Sra, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 144, 2787 (2016)), but not a length: in log-brightness logcosh(u/2)\sqrt{\log\cosh(u/2)} is strictly concave, so splitting a monotone interval gives a larger sum than comparing its ends. Accumulated over four thousand small steps and divided by the direct comparison, it gives 1.020, 1.074, 1.229, 1.396 and 1.555 at log-contrasts 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8; the Riemannian control gives 1.000 every time. DERIVED (identity checked to twenty digits; script NONRIEMANN-WHERE-01).

The same balance runs through colour. For two colour channels the share balance is exactly the Smith point Γ\Gamma, Hilbert’s projective distance between two mixtures is exactly the peel distance |lnz−lnz′||\ln z - \ln z'|, and the Schrödinger chromatic angle φ\varphi obeys cosφ=Γ\cos\varphi = \Gamma, checked on 20,000 pairs (COLOUR-PEEL-01, votkp-lean, research of 10 November 2026). At the wall cosφ=1/2\cos\varphi = 1/\sqrt2, so the wall sits at the chromatic angle 45∘45^\circ, the same 45∘45^\circ at which a ball face reaches its boundary in Section 2. DERIVED.

Human colour perception shows the same diminishing returns: large colour differences are judged smaller than the sum of the small ones, which no Riemannian colour space allows (R. Bujack et al., “The non-Riemannian nature of perceptual color space”, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. 119, e2119753119 (2022)). On the Los Alamos judgment data my ledger curve does not beat the logarithm everywhere: the logarithm wins on grey by +0.000805+0.000805 nats per response (95% interval +0.00027+0.00027 to +0.00136+0.00136), the ledger curve has a small green–pink advantage of −0.000401-0.000401, and the blue–orange whole-triad interval spans zero (Colour Selects the Leader v1.2, §5). MEASURED (their data, my fits). The ledger and human vision share a shape; this is an analogy, not a model of how the eye sees.

Her notebook terms, read as the peel

Elizabeth’s notebook pages are hers. Read in her terms they name the same objects as the peel; the translation is mine and is marked.

Matter and memory. She writes matter as positive, giving shell and sections, and memory as negative, the recipe; matter and memory together make the firework. I write the same split in my two books: the positive book E+=(ΣIE)2E^+ = (\Sigma IE)^2 is the shell, and the negative book E−=(ΔIE)2E^- = (\Delta IE)^2 is the record of the step.

The drum. Her page reads: to go from 3 : 7 to 10 requires a 4 drum to get 3 to activate 7. For the pair 3 and 7, the 4 is the difference and the 10 is the sum, so Γ=7−37+3=410,E−E+=16100.\Gamma = \frac{7-3}{7+3} = \frac{4}{10},\qquad \frac{E^-}{E^+} = \frac{16}{100}. Her drum is the difference face and her ten is the sum face: this is my reflection written in her own terms. DERIVED.

The monad at the midpoint. I place the monad — the still point of a step — at the midpoint of the pair. For 3 and 7 the midpoint is 5 and half the gap is 2, so Γ=2/5\Gamma = 2/5: the reflection is half the gap measured against the midpoint, and the stillness sits exactly in the middle, as Russell’s fulcrum does.

The pilot hole. In her drawing a memory photon runs ahead from A to B, finds the best path, and returns to A before matter makes the run. A wave that goes out and comes back is a reflection, and Γ\Gamma is a reflection coefficient. Her picture reads Γ\Gamma as the returning echo that sets the path. RECOGNISED as a structural reading.

Her gap ladder. She writes ratios by gap, 2 : 1, 4 : 1, 6 : 1, 8 : 1, with the gap as the oxygen amount, running from “easier” at 2 to “harder” at 10, and 1 : 1 as “furthest away from itself”. Read as peel steps zz:

Her ratio Γ2\Gamma^2 Side of the wall
1 : 1 0 matched, nothing reflected
2 : 1 0.111 inside
4 : 1 0.360 inside
6 : 1 0.510 outside
8 : 1 0.605 outside

The wall at 5.83 falls between her 4 and her 6; her page marks 2 as easier and 10 as harder. DERIVED as a structural match, not a test. Her page calls kindling a twin segment with many gaps and firewood segments with few, and her grid runs in columns headed 3, 7 and 9. I read this, as my interpretation, through her prime work: those are last digits of primes above 5, and a twin segment would be a twin-prime gap of 2, her tinder. Her even ladder is not ordinary fuel chemistry: alkanes take (3n+1)/2(3n+1)/2 oxygen molecules per fuel molecule (2, 3.5, 5, 6.5, 8 from methane to pentane), so the two ladders meet only at methane’s 2 : 1 and pentane’s 8 : 1.

Fastest or maximum energy. She writes that efficiency is fastest or maximum energy, and cannot be both. For steady-running heat engines this is a known trade-off: power and efficiency cannot both be maximised (Shiraishi, Saito and Tasaki 2016; Pietzonka and Seifert 2018), and a recent Pareto-front result bounds the efficiency at maximum power by one half of the maximum efficiency, with zero power at maximum efficiency. Whether that one half and my half-power wall are the same line is OPEN, untested.

Questions she asked me in our conversation, answered. Layered: yes — the shells are layered, and each peel step goes from one layer to the next. Moving in parallel like conveyor belts: nothing in the data shows it yet; it is a picture to test. An inserted charge: yes — each removal leaves the ion one charge more positive, which pulls every remaining electron in and restructures the whole at every step. “Too close to the ceiling”: a step that jumps too far; past a ratio of 5.83 the loop cannot close, and the steps that do this are the breaks into a closed inner core. The speed of light and the charge: not the same thing, but they meet in one number, the fine-structure constant α≈1/137\alpha\approx1/137 — the charge squared over the speed of light and Planck’s constant — which enters this paper as the (Zα)2(Z\alpha)^2 spinor correction of the heavy hydrogen-like ions. The squaring in my formulas turns a strength into an energy, which is why one half is the line.

OPEN. The preregistered blind colour test — Elizabeth’s colour readings scored against the wall circle before either of us sees the other’s calls — still needs her readings.

What survives the passage from a peel to a laboratory reading?

HYPOTHESIS. “The vector determines the direction, that may be decay.” In the element work a direction has to say what is ordered: the two thresholds of one atom, the same-charge thresholds of two isobars, the endpoints of an oriented crystal walk, or the polarisation and frequency of a light probe. Each ordering permits an explicit reversal experiment. The operations act on different spaces, so a sign that survives one operation can reverse under another. The test is to write the observation map and identify what survives it. I start from the intrinsic record; ångströms, electronvolts and laboratory time enter only where a crystallographic, mass or spectral datum is supplied.

An internal face, a junction, a current

DERIVED. The internal peel compares two successive removal thresholds. A junction compares the clocks on opposing sites. For identical clocks the junction ratio is one and its scalar reflection is zero, whatever the internal helium-core opening. In the original finite hydrogen-cell construction, sodium’s internal L opening on an exterior port gave a weakest squared link of about 0.000292; keeping that clock inside and matching the exterior clocks gave about 0.000865. Argon’s corresponding L-opening calculation changed from 0.000648 to 0.000872 (its first ordinary step, from 0.000804 to 0.000874), and the all-matched control gave 0.000876 in both conventions, against the all-ones reference 0.000875546. Putting the atom’s peel ratio on the faces had made sodium look less connected than argon; moving it inside the ball closes about 98% of that gap, and every row stays below 1/121/12. These are numerical outputs of the specified two-level cell. They test whether a clock was attached to the correct link; they do not supply the bands or the filling of sodium metal.

DERIVED. For an orthogonal occupied projector P=P2=P†P = P^2 = P^\dagger, choose mutually orthogonal, complete site projectors Πi\Pi_i. Put Pij=ΠiPΠjP_{ij} = \Pi_iP\Pi_j, Ci=PiiC_i = P_{ii} on its site, and Xij=Tr(PijPji)X_{ij} = \operatorname{Tr}(P_{ij}P_{ji}). The diagonal block of P2=PP^2 = P gives an exact budget, Bi=Tr(Ci−Ci2)=∑j≠iXij.B_i = \operatorname{Tr}\big(C_i - C_i^2\big) = \sum_{j\ne i}X_{ij}. If a shell contains nn equivalent neighbours, the strict per-neighbour condition Xij>Bi/(3n)X_{ij}>B_i/(3n) says exactly that more than one third of the off-site weight lies on that shell. For inequivalent neighbours the actual shell sum is required, and the normalised share needs Bi>0B_i>0. The one-third criterion is an assigned cutoff. A claim about a macroscopic percolation transition would need an independently defined network, conducting constituents, a disorder ensemble and a conductivity observable.

RECOGNISED. This budget is the chemists’ delocalisation sum rule. Tr(Ci−Ci2)\operatorname{Tr}(C_i-C_i^2) is the variance of the number of electrons on site ii, and ∥Pij∥2\|P_{ij}\|^2 is half the delocalisation index between sites ii and jj per spin — the quantity behind Bader’s atoms-in-molecules analysis and the Wiberg–Mayer bond orders. Dividing the nearest shell’s share by the whole budget is the step I add; I found no earlier source that does it. A half-filled chain gives exactly 8/π2=0.8118/\pi^2 = 0.811 (checked: 0.81056934 against 0.81056947).

DERIVED, false controls. For one spin-degenerate orbital per site in the translation-invariant band model with per-spin filling 0<f<10<f<1, the magnitude of a separated per-spin matrix element cannot exceed ff by the triangle inequality on its Fourier sum. Thus Xij≤2f2X_{ij}\le2f^2 and Bi=2f(1−f)B_i = 2f(1-f). For eight neighbours the nearest-shell fraction is at most 8f/(1−f)8f/(1-f), which cannot exceed one third if f≤1/25f\le1/25, even though the band is partly filled (Lean: dilute_bcc_fails). Conversely, a filled, gapped bonding-band example has strong nearest-shell concentration, and passes more strongly as the gap grows while its absolute link weight falls. In the half-filled bcc example the link weight 0.0333 exceeds its 1/481/48 cutoff. Together these rule out inferring conductivity from this criterion alone. What it measures is the spatial distribution of occupied-state sharing. So I keep three separate readings for every junction: the absolute shared weight, the fraction carried by each neighbour shell, and a bulk transport response.

From a spatial distribution to a projector differential

DERIVED, with crystallographic inputs. In the rubidium and krypton calculation a site is a real-space Wigner–Seitz cell. For a supercell translation class RR the two-spin squared weight XRX_R obeys ∑RXR=ν\sum_RX_R = \nu, where ν=1\nu = 1 for the chosen outer rubidium band and ν=8\nu = 8 for the chosen krypton valence subspace. The spatial partition assigns each point the position of its site’s centre. With all tied shortest Cartesian images averaged, the per-electron tensor is Λabc=12ν∑RXR⟨RaRb⟩shortest.\Lambda^c_{ab} = \frac{1}{2\nu}\sum_RX_R\,\big\langle R_aR_b\big\rangle_{\text{shortest}}. Intracell structure contributes zero at R=0R = 0 by this convention. The lattice parameters are 5.700 Å for bcc rubidium (297 K crystallographic input) and 5.721 Å for fcc krypton (58 K input); the calculation uses fixed structures and zero-temperature occupation, and the temperatures identify the structural sources, not a matched thermal experiment. For any position operator constant on each site, Var(X)=12∑ij∥Pij∥2(xi−xj)2,\operatorname{Var}(X) = \tfrac12\sum_{ij}\|P_{ij}\|^2(x_i-x_j)^2, the second moment of the same off-site weights whose zeroth moment is the shell fraction.

Light as a probe with a specified channel

MEASURED AND DERIVED. The helium-core crossing between carbon and nitrogen gives a direct opportunity to test the atomic loop wall: carbon’s and nitrogen’s helium-core openings have opposite equal-face classifications. On a common transition of their lithium-like ions, published integrated resonance strengths are 0.483±0.100.483\pm0.10 and 0.413±0.070.413\pm0.07, and their quoted intervals overlap. Carbon and boron were measured at ALS, nitrogen and oxygen at SOLEIL, so a fitted wall step is confounded with facility. A separate single-facility electron-impact experiment detected an inner-shell excitation contribution on both sides, so loss of this excitation channel on crossing is ruled out. Single-ion measurements cannot implement the mixed carbon–nitrogen two-face construction without a physical coupling and a joint readout. An independent single-facility sequence with a predeclared effect size, normalisation and comparison to a smooth baseline is a concrete discriminating test. (Müller et al. 2009; Al Shorman et al. 2013; McLaughlin et al. 2017; Crandall et al. 1979.)

The gap needs a position, a direction and a phase

DERIVED from measured structures. In dhcp neodymium the two crystallographic cages have identical lists of twelve distances, zero first vector sums and equal second-moment tensors. One contains six antipodal bond pairs and the other three. A basal third angular moment separates them, with squared magnitudes 0 and 1/1081/108 in the documented dimensionless convention. Polarised-neutron measurements found their susceptibilities agree above 40 K but differ below 19.9 K. The geometry separates the sites at both temperatures; extracting a magnetic transition temperature would need an electronic and thermal model. In coexisting high-pressure ytterbium phases at 30.28 and 31.28 GPa, measured refinements give a smaller volume per atom in hcp but a longer shortest contact than bcc, and the signs survive three quoted lattice-parameter widths in both cells. These controls rule out reconstructing a unique gap geometry from total volume or from an atom’s scalar peel face alone. (Moon et al. 1983; Storm et al. 2026.)

In the specified handed high-pressure ytterbium refinement the average of χ\chi over all 64 shortest three-step walks vanishes, while the dimensionless third moment ⟨(χ/Vatom)3⟩=−3/128\langle(\chi/V_{\text{atom}})^3\rangle = -3/128 changes sign under reflection. Powder diffraction supplies an allowed enantiomorphic model and cannot by itself establish the absolute hand of a specimen. A finite contact walk or a screw closed only modulo a translation does not define a classical knot polynomial; a defined embedded closure and invariance under its allowed changes are required on the Volume of the Knot Potential side.

Where the wall can be tested

The elemental ladders leave a window in which every cutoff classifies the archived steps alike. The geometry fixes one exact number inside it. Four settings now sit inside that window and can ask what the geometry predicts that its neighbours do not: a resolved oxygen channel, a theory-only hydrogen-like pair, a specified optical return, and francium.

For consecutive positive removal energies, reversing their order changes the sign of Γ\Gamma and keeps Γ2\Gamma^2. On a forward equal-face step, Γ2=12\Gamma^2 = \tfrac12 gives the exact geometric wall w=3+22w = 3+2\sqrt2; comparing a tabulated ratio with ww is fully defined, including the equality case. A finite collection of mixed historical inputs also leaves freedom in the law that combines them: a strictly increasing piecewise map can fix every sampled reflection power, preserve every historical paired decision and still move the diagonal cutoff within the gap. A new setting and an independently observed outcome have different experimental roles from the historical table.

Francium

Francium is the one element whose ordinary core opening straddles the wall on present data. The registered statement and the failed extrapolation are both in The element test above. Where the vector reaches nuclear decay

HYPOTHESIS and its falsifier. “The vector determines the direction, that may be decay.” Three different directions can be tested. Does the next ionisation move two isobars closer together or farther apart in ground mass? Which is heavier after many removals? Does a specific initial state actually decay, and at what rate? Each question admits its own counterexample. A wrong signed mass increment would challenge the first mapping. Correct increments can accumulate on opposite sides of a different starting mass. An energetically permitted transition can be too slow to detect on a particular experimental timescale. The distinctions become measurable in three isotope pairs.

Reading. The mathematically strongest link with “that may be decay” is constructive. The vector with its first threshold rebuilds each electronic energy. Comparing two rebuilt ladders reproduces the charge-dependent part of a mass difference. The ground-mass difference then locates a possible change in energetic direction. A spatial hand, an order sense, a dielectric response, an ordering of nuclear masses and an observed event rate need different measurements, and keeping them apart lets an experiment contradict one proposed correspondence while leaving the independently tested ones intact.

From a direction to a calibrated prediction

The charge-ladder experiment sharpens the connection to decay. Suppose each energy or other positive clock is a vertex of a finite graph, and a measured edge supplies zuv>0z_{uv}>0 with an orientation from uu to vv. I ask whether there are positive vertex clocks xvx_v with zuv=xv/xuz_{uv} = x_v/x_u on every measured edge. This is the scalar reconstruction problem for the intrinsic clock readings; no spacing in laboratory metres or seconds has entered.

DERIVED — reconstruction. Set buv=lnzuvb_{uv} = \ln z_{uv}, with bvu=−buvb_{vu} = -b_{uv}. Vertex clocks exist exactly when the signed bb’s sum to zero on every cycle. Necessity follows by telescoping. For sufficiency, choose one root in each connected component, give it an arbitrary log-clock and propagate by summing bb along a spanning tree; any extra edge closes one fundamental cycle, and its zero sum makes the propagated values satisfy that edge. Subtracting any two solutions, the log-clock difference is constant on every component: exactly one free positive multiplier per component, including an isolated vertex. An independently calibrated edge joining two components fixes their relative multiplier, and a single absolute anchor then fixes both. A non-trivial measured cycle residual falsifies the scalar exact-difference premise for that set of edges. A concrete false control: three successive oriented ratios 2, 3, 1/5 have product 6/5, which forbids scalar clock potentials although every individual reflection is well defined. Statistical use needs correlations propagated, especially when two edges share a threshold. Non-commuting transport around a loop is an additional observation and does not satisfy this scalar hypothesis in general — which is exactly where my loop wall lives. A peel ladder is a coboundary; a loop with a non-trivial commutator is not.

What would make the vector a volume?

DERIVED — a failure of identification. Even the three lengths of three incident unit directions do not determine a volume. Take v1=e1v_1 = e_1, v2=e2v_2 = e_2 and v3=cosαe1+sinαe3v_3 = \cos\alpha\,e_1+\sin\alpha\,e_3 in a positive-definite comparison space. The three lengths stay one, while their signed volume is sinα\sin\alpha, so its magnitude runs from zero to one and its sign can reverse. The Gram determinant is sin2α\sin^2\alpha and misses the hand. A single chain of relative scalar steps carries still less incidence information. The example refutes a universal length-only reconstruction by exhibiting admissible inputs that cannot be told apart. It uses a finite comparison space; my intrinsic tensor can have a different domain, signature or degeneracy.

HYPOTHESIS — a constructive way to ask my question. Choose three independently addressable intrinsic perturbations at a junction. Specify the observed state or projector, establish that the three changes are linearly independent in the retained quotient, and state a volume functional and an orientation convention on that space. A positive Gram form on their span would define a magnitude detG\sqrt{\det G}; a signed three-form would also record an orientation. A degenerate form calls for its null directions to be identified, and an indefinite form needs its own convention. Then vary the geometry while keeping the scalar peel ladder fixed. Neodymium’s inequivalent sites give a target with shared radial information; the screw hand in β-manganese gives a target with opposite spatial parity. The hypothesis gains content if an independently specified intrinsic reading predicts the measured difference on withheld sites or hands after the scalar inputs are matched. Failure places the missing information in the chosen projector, directions, volume functional or observation rule, and telling which needs all four recorded.

HYPOTHESIS — light as the leader. The full Dirac Time pump–remove–probe construction suggests a fair intervention. Prepare matched initial populations; drive two arms with the same deposited energy, spectrum, temperature and final scalar thresholds, varying only their order or relative phase. Remove the pump and compare a prespecified polarisation-resolved or time-resolved readout. Define the sign, timing window, repeatability and blinded null arm before acquisition. A coherent phase witness that reverses on the specified operation and survives matched heating would show a retained light-path record in that preparation. If a phase-scrambled control reproduces the signal within the preregistered sensitivity, that witness fails this way. A light-controlled volume claim also needs an independently measured change in the proposed volume observable; colour alone cannot establish it.

Direction: the even half and the odd half

My work began with questions about Walter Russell, Tesla and the periodic table, and this paper loops back to them. Russell’s two-column method carried every quantity that stays the same under a mirror and lost every quantity that flips. My reading of Russell separates the two books by whether something stays or flips on crossing a wall. The peel ledger keeps both halves: Γ2\Gamma^2 and the wall classification are the even half; the sign of Γ\Gamma is the odd half under reversing the peel. That reading earns a precise meaning only after the operation is named.

Reversing the ordered pair of positive thresholds sends z↦1/zz\mapsto1/z, r↦−rr\mapsto-r and Γ↦−Γ\Gamma\mapsto-\Gamma, and fixes Γ2\Gamma^2. Replacing a loop flux by its negative fixes ReW\operatorname{Re}W and reverses ImW\operatorname{Im}W. A real crystal supplies the spatial half. β-manganese comes in two mirror crystals, space groups P4132P4_132 and P4332P4_332. Its shortest-contact screw orbit (step 2.3743 Å) gives a four-site path with screw sign χ=(d0×d1)⋅d2=+9.9306\chi = (d_0\times d_1)\cdot d_2 = +9.9306 Å³. Mirroring space flips the sign; reversing the four-site ordering keeps it, because that reversal is an even permutation (Lean: chi_reverse, chi_mirror).

Reverse the order of the record flips stays (+9.9306 Å³) stays (+11.1638 Å³) stays (+21.2240 Å³)
Mirror the crystal stays flips flips (−11.1638 Å³) flips (−21.2240 Å³)

Trigonal selenium (P3121P3_121, crystal record 1534711, bond 2.30066 Å) is a different screw: a three-fold helix rather than β-manganese’s four-fold one. It obeys the same law, and so does trigonal tellurium (P3121P3_121, record 2020222, bond 2.8345 Å); an independently refined P3221P3_221 tellurium crystal gives −21.990034-21.990034 Å³. In Barron’s terms the screw sign is a true-chirality quantity: odd under a mirror, even under time reversal. My peel reflection is the opposite kind. Tellurium’s handedness has been measured directly by resonant X-ray diffraction (Tanaka et al. 2010); current-induced magnetisation has been observed in trigonal tellurium (Furukawa et al. 2017). Closing the β-manganese screw path around one lattice period gives an unknot for both hands. An unframed knot polynomial of that closure cannot tell them apart, but the framed winding and the local sign can. The knot side of VOTKP needs a closed path that keeps that sign. A signed volume distinguishes hands for a specified sample geometry; it does not establish a torus-knot type for a periodically continued path until its closure, ambient space and equivalence moves are supplied.

The spinor-peel recovery makes the same split in an operator. On the three-mode loop the energy ledger sees ReW\operatorname{Re}W — even, like Γ2\Gamma^2 — and the directional test sees ImW\operatorname{Im}W — odd, like the sign of Γ\Gamma and the screw sign. Electric charge stays invariant under ordinary spatial reflection, while charge conjugation reverses it; calling both “mirror” would make a historical test ambiguous.

Russell’s octave and his iron columns

The octave. Russell’s octave reads conventional valence magnitudes 1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 in the simplest main-group period pattern. The atomic anion readout gives an independent comparison. In the retained table oxygen has IE1/EA≃9.320IE_1/EA\simeq9.320, outside the wall; sulfur, selenium and tellurium have about 4.988, 4.826 and 4.571, inside, and on the provisional polonium affinity polonium joins them inside at 5.703. Fluorine’s value near 5.123 is inside while lithium’s near 8.724 is outside, although the octave pairs their unit magnitudes. Lithium with fluorine, beryllium with oxygen and boron with nitrogen agree in conventional valence magnitude under the short-period pairing, yet each pair straddles the helium-core opening wall. A donor–acceptor test also differs from either isolated-atom rung: lithium’s ionisation energy over fluorine’s affinity gives about 1.585, an energy comparison before binding, environment or crystal relaxation. Russell’s historical sorting remains a claim about the sampled plates until the transformation, outcome and uncertainty are coded across the whole 386-entry ledger. The element-focused audit covers 132 of 585 original claim and law positions. RECOGNISED.

The parity pilot. In a grade-blinded spatial-inversion pilot, two AI raters coded 24 masked Russell verdicts and agreed on 23; of the 20 agreed-even claims, 10 were true and 10 false. “Even implies true” failed this way. A valid test has to allow “neither”: a numerical mass-ratio error, for example, does not by itself change sign under a specified mirror.

The three iron columns. On printed page 204 of The Universal One (1926), each of Russell’s three columns — “iron”, “recent” and “remote” — holds 23 wavelengths. An unshifted ±0.20 Å air-wavelength search against observed neutral-iron lines gives 21 of 23, 20 of 23 and 19 of 23. Moving the whole set of 23 together by every integer displacement from −50 to −5 and +5 to +50 Å gives median hits of 7, 5 and 5 and maxima of 12, 12 and 10: no translated list scores as well as the original, a descriptive tail fraction of 1/93 in each column. A separate extraction of Nave et al.’s laboratory line table reproduces the three counts, and ionised iron gives only 2, 4 and 2. Kayser’s 1910 comparison prints, in each column, at least one neutral-iron line whose old Rowland-scale wavelength rounds to Russell’s tenth of an ångström; Russell was working from real iron spectra of his day, though his actual source is unknown. His remote line at 5269.6 Å coincides, to his printed precision, with the solar Fraunhofer E line identified as iron at 5269.551 Å in Abbot’s The Sun (1911). These counts locate ordinary iron-line coincidences in all three columns. MEASURED / RECOGNISED. They do not identify every line uniquely, establish atomic ancestry or score Russell’s whole record: the “recent” and “remote” labels as different atomic ancestors get no support from wavelengths alone, and that interpretation stays open in the ledger. The recount of the three numbers from the committed line table was repeated independently; the re-extraction from the 1926 plate and the NIST list has its own provenance.

The vacancies. Russell’s 1926 plate places vacancies at the later technetium, promethium, astatine and francium positions. Bohr’s 1922 plate already shows those vacancies, and Russell also leaves surplus places. The dates credit an early correct placement where supported and leave historical priority as a separate claim.

What Russell saw rightly. Read through the peel, Russell’s two halves are real: what stays under a mirror and what flips are carried separately, and the wall reads only the even half. His octave is not the wall, but his oxygen–fluorine turn sits where the anion rungs cross from outside to inside. His iron was iron. And his fulcrum — the stillness at the centre of two opposed flows — is the midpoint of my peel step.

Two Russell originals and the Galactic filament model

My original September study gives an auditable count: 282 entries from The Universal One and 104 from The Genero-Radiative Concept, plus 199 separately graded “laws”. Its oscillator reconstruction takes paired stores on a fixed energy budget. Parallel and antiparallel currents furnish a controlled force-sign example once geometry and current directions are specified — the original Maxwell-stress reading that opposed flows expand and parallel flows attract, which I believe connects decay, the elements and time, and which stays a hypothesis here. The orbit comparison has a local quantitative form. In the periapsis calculation, the nearly circular Schwarzschild radial-to-orbital frequency ratio satisfies κr2/Ω2=1−6GM/(c2r)\kappa_r^2/\Omega^2 = 1-6GM/(c^2r); matching the Newtonian power-law small-oscillation result 3−p3-p defines peff=2+6GM/(c2r)p_{\text{eff}} = 2+6GM/(c^2r), which reaches three at the innermost stable circular orbit. That concerns a local ratio of frequencies; it gives neither a global inverse-cube force nor a law under which every orbit spirals at that radius. Russell, Corrected (November) redraws seven plates and itself names classification of the full ledger as the outstanding test of Plate II.

The Galactic source is a separate paper of mine dated 17 September 2026 (later revised under a different title), A Five-Dimensional Non-Normal Stability Operator with Gradient-Driven Interface Coupling for Zero-Precursor Filamentary Fractures. Its minimal five-coordinate realisation depends on the proposed shape, shear and refraction sector hypotheses. Its most transferable calculation lies on a two-dimensional invariant block. Put J=bI+μNJ = bI+\mu N, N12=1N_{12} = 1, N2=0N^2 = 0, b>0b>0. Then ∥e−Jt∥2=e−bt4+|μ|2t2+|μ|t2.\big\|e^{-Jt}\big\|_2 = e^{-bt}\,\frac{\sqrt{4+|\mu|^2t^2}+|\mu|t}{2}. With κ=|μ|/b\kappa = |\mu|/b, transient gain above one occurs exactly at κ>2\kappa>2 for the induced Euclidean norm, although both generator eigenvalues have real part −b-b. For κ>2\kappa>2 the maximum is at t*=κ2−4/|μ|t_* = \sqrt{\kappa^2-4}/|\mu|. The norm is an amplitude gain; its square is the maximal energy gain for an optimally aligned unit input, which matters when comparing the rupture threshold to an energy. Its right-half-plane condition also needs the sign convention for the generator −K-K throughout; the stable decay matrix KK itself has positive eigenvalues here. The application to the Galactic Centre Snake, G359.1−0.2, adds an impactor, an initial direction, a rupture ceiling, and competing radiation and passage times; the paper names pulsar proper motion, the minor kink’s opposite spectral-index gradient and an advance modal precursor as tests. The Jordan-block calculation shows how a stable spectrum can coexist with transient gain; it cannot identify the origin of an observed kink by itself. A second exact connection to Dirac Time is that an isolated spectral cluster has a contour projector whose rank persists along a continuous path while the contour stays gapped. Equating the Galactic ratio |μ|/b|\mu|/b with an atomic IEk+1/IEkIE_{k+1}/IE_k would add a hypothesis the sources do not calibrate.

The Standard Model ball and the nucleus

My construction. Fix a common comparison energy E≥mE\ge m in units c=1c = 1. A massive particle can be given rapidity η=arcosh(E/m)\eta = \operatorname{arcosh}(E/m) and radial position ρ=tanh(η/2)\rho = \tanh(\eta/2) in a velocity ball, so equal radii correspond to equal ratios E/mE/m under this display convention. For eη=5e^\eta = 5 the Lorentz factor is 13/5, the speed 12/13 and the radial coordinate 2/3. This coordinate uses half the rapidity; the face apex uses a quarter of the logarithmic step. Fixing the comparison energy is indispensable: changing it moves every massive entry and decides which are admissible. For the proper orthochronous Lorentz group, a massive rest momentum has rotational little group SO(3)SO(3) with double cover SU(2)SU(2); at a null momentum the little group is locally the Euclidean group in two dimensions, whose translations act trivially in the familiar finite-helicity representations. These statements clarify the spin labels the construction puts on the ball; they do not produce particle masses, forces or a nuclear binding calculation.

The study tested two readings of six tree directions. As colour weights, projecting ±ei\pm e_i onto the plane perpendicular to (1,1,1)(1,1,1) gives the two triples of opposite weights of 3⊕3‾3\oplus\bar3; the differences ei−eje_i-e_j give the six non-zero roots, and the adjoint has two more zero-weight directions. A diagram reproducing weights leaves the gauge coupling and dynamics unspecified. As generation assignments, whole-generation integer boost levels failed the attempted fit. The 48 integral quaternions of norm five form six packets of eight; reading 48 as three packets of sixteen fermionic states adds counting conventions, including a right-handed neutrino per generation, and equality of counts cannot decide between two partitions. The charged-lepton Koide input gives Q=0.666664463Q = 0.666664463 and cos2θ=1/(3Q)≃0.500001652\cos^2\theta = 1/(3Q)\simeq0.500001652. A deliberate search found no exact cone hit among 117,186 tree nodes through depth seven, or among 23,100 turn axes through depth six. Lab-frame velocity directions converge in three examined examples about as e−ηe^{-\eta}; a body-fixed spin frame does not in general freeze along a non-straight end. A prediction connecting the ball to particles needs an invariant independent of the observer’s frame and mass evaluation scale.

For an isotope with mass number AA and atomic number ZZ, the central bookkeeping is ZZ protons and A−ZA-Z neutrons; net valence-flavour counts are u=A+Zu = A+Z and d=2A−Zd = 2A-Z. Ordinary electron removal changes ionic charge and keeps these nuclear labels, provided there is no nuclear reaction. A nuclear count does not locate individual quarks on six geometric ports. It gives a simple falsifier: two isotopes of one element have the same electron count at the same ionic charge and different neutron counts, and a picture assigning both the same nuclear trait vector would lose a measured distinction.

The recovered spinor peel

Take a three-site Hermitian loop with hopping modulus JJ and oriented product W=J3eiΦW = J^3e^{i\Phi}. Its characteristic polynomial λ3−3J2λ−2J3cosΦ\lambda^3-3J^2\lambda-2J^3\cos\Phi gives identical spectra at opposite phases, yet the leading probability difference is P(1→2)−P(2→1)=2Im(W)t3+O(t4)P(1\to2)-P(2\to1) = 2\operatorname{Im}(W)\,t^3+O(t^4). At Φ=±π/2\Phi = \pm\pi/2 and t=2π/(33J)t = 2\pi/(3\sqrt3J) one gets opposite perfect cycles — a known chiral quantum walk (Zimborás et al. 2013), used here to control a question about peeling. After eliminating site three the remaining effective hopping is J+J2e−iΦ/EJ+J^2e^{-i\Phi}/E with diagonal correction J2/EJ^2/E, for E≠0E\ne0: the direction lost by comparing energies alone survives in an effective operator that keeps the phase. The free flat shifted torus is a negative control: for modes (m,n)(m,n), D2=(2π)2[(m+α)2+(n+β)2]D^2 = (2\pi)^2[(m+\alpha)^2+(n+\beta)^2], anticommutation with σ3\sigma_3 pairs the non-zero eigenvalues about zero, and the ordinary eta invariant vanishes; integer shifts allow a kernel, which the reduced eta convention includes separately. A non-zero asymmetry claim needs an operator or boundary condition that actually breaks the pairing.

Proposed decisive experiment. Prepare cells with separately specified internal clocks and matched external clocks. Keep coordination, filling, basis, hopping and size extrapolation explicit. Compare an open-shell metal, a filled gapped insulator and an atomic-limit insulator with the same measurement and current-response protocol. Predict before the comparison which link-weight moments and which dynamical observables will order the materials. The filled-band control already rules out “passes the link threshold” as a sufficient condition for metallic conduction. A prediction that survives these controls would connect a model of the gap to a material observation and keep the full audit of what was tried.

Reproduction. The archived hydrogen gap check, layer-clock check, seven-ball check, container check and spinor-recovery check were executed for this edition. The first three printed “all hold”; the container printed its one killed closed-boundary control; the spinor check returned the leading-direction, cycle, Schur and flat-torus controls with sampled memory residual about 5.04×10−75.04\times10^{-7}. The tree check, after a one-character string repair in a scratch copy, reproduced the 7.0×10−57.0\times10^{-5} twin discrepancy, the 2log32\log3 path length and the failed equality control.

The November working ledger and its open decisions

My dated notes ask how a hypersurface peels itself, how a leading vector meets a covector at the cut, whether the space between atoms sets the lattice, how a ground can hold or move charge, how heating and cooling build structure, whether light guides the electronic response, and whether a directed change can select a decay. They put colour, superfluidity, conductivity and differential response to light on the agenda. My standing directions, in my words, are these: the way the hypersurface peels itself is where I want to look; conductivity or not is the key in all elements, set by the electron, with light as its twin guiding it; the space between atoms is the non-conductive part, like ground or the vacuum, and it varies with each element’s lattice spacing; heat to cold is what forms matter into a lattice; time decides which branch gets cut at the hypersurface; the vector determines the direction, and that may be decay. Behind all of it is my quest: whether memory can make electricity faster. And the best question from those days stays open at the head of this ledger: when the needle swings, what does it keep? The checks below keep apart a proposed mechanism, a number inferred by an effective model and a laboratory observation.

The volume-fraction proxy and the intrinsic face

DERIVED. The November working sheet explores the proxy E=1−(rcov/rroom)3E = 1-(r_{\text{cov}}/r_{\text{room}})^3, where rroomr_{\text{room}} comes from the observed per-atom volume and rcovr_{\text{cov}} from a chosen covalent-radius convention. The corresponding ratio zE=1/(1−E)z_E = 1/(1-E) has ΓE=E/(2−E)\Gamma_E = E/(2-E), so E=2/3E = 2/3 gives zE=3z_E = 3 and ΓE=1/2\Gamma_E = 1/2. This is a valid re-expression of the proxy, and it is different from the internal clock IEk+1/IEkIE_{k+1}/IE_k, the face apex tanh(r/4)\tanh(r/4), the junction mismatch and the off-site projector weight. The 2/32/3 empty-fraction line and the 3+223+2\sqrt2 equal-face loop wall are separate thresholds. Ground-state tables and a chosen radius prescription cannot fix the microscopic contents of an interstitial region.

RECOGNISED, archived results. The 81-row current-data sheet has one exception at the fixed 2/32/3 line (boron) and two at 0.63 (arsenic, polonium). On 35 metals the empty fraction and log DC conductivity have Spearman correlation only +0.072; the same fraction with optical phase has about +0.78. A phase cutoff at 0.661 rad separates the 41 members of one visible-optics sample; it was fitted on that sample. Measured pressure, density and phase changes give harder tests: the proxy catches the silicon and germanium melting changes in the supplied density brackets; fluid hydrogen and dense xenon put the observed metallisation close to the competing Herzfeld estimate; and expanded alkalis stay metallic beyond the proposed density line. A same-material phase comparison controls for the isolated-atom ladder. A second proxy built from static polarisability is a distinct model.

RECOGNISED, archived results. The signed optical-track area is clockwise in 39 of 41 first-set cases. The independent 60-material test records 56 clockwise, three counterclockwise and one flat. The fixed sign-wall optical metal classifier misses 25 of 41 and failed this way. Family-level outlier rates run from about 0.02 in the f-block lanthanum-to-lutetium group to 0.44 in zinc–cadmium–mercury. Scalar-relativistic contraction correlates with one heavy-element margin, while its pooled relation to outlier rate is weak and several computations failed to converge. The open ledger keeps every excluded run and every optical, proxy and radius convention. Colour is wavelength-, polarisation-, surface- and phase-dependent, while the free-atom threshold is shared across these conditions.

Further work kept from the harness

Archived line Surviving statement and its boundary
Knot census and cap filling The historical replay reports 353/251 pairs against printed 354/253 under its two counts. Necessary cap-fill bounds survived while candidate exact laws failed. Any new exact fill rule must beat the archived 330-case controls.
Tree turning and opposed controls At depth parameter 10910^9 the twin-chain turn was still changing beyond the prespecified tolerance. Of 24 runnable opposite controls, 13 fired and 11 did not; five were unrunnable and four skipped. Nulls, skipped tests and inconclusive runs have separate records. Over all words up to length 10, the two-step group has 0 elliptic words at the wall and outside, and 240 inside.
Band mean, gap and depth The band-end exit relation and the shared exponential law per unit length have different hypotheses from equality per pass. The archived per-pass equality occurs at one special ratio, about 6.26913.
Lattice assemblies Prescribed six axial, eight diagonal and twelve face directions generate simple-cubic, bcc and fcc assemblies under the recorded rules. Their ability to realise a lattice once directions are supplied does not predict which directions a real element selects.
Neutrino and truncated chains In the specified two-moment closure one exceptional-point condition matches the loop wall exactly; extending to the full chain moves the threshold. That comparison tests the truncation and does not calibrate an atomic speed. My neutrino papers, The Neutrinos at the Wall and When the Neutrinos Leave, share the wall at this level, and the link is a lead.
Provenance and build The original VOTKP root build, the separate Two Trees build and the later element certificates have distinct counts and dependency closures. The gathered November folder provides a file-level checksum index for recovered material.

What only this work has

Stated plainly, these are the results that are mine and that I have not found elsewhere:

  1. An exact wall from geometry, not a fit. 3+223+2\sqrt2 comes from asking when two faces at a right angle stop closing a loop, and of the two named extensions of the two-face rule — sum form and product form — it is the one equal-face cutoff for which they agree (Lean-proved).
  2. The data window that contains it. Every classification from hydrogen to astatine survives only for cutoffs in [5.80790,5.86654)[5.80790, 5.86654), silver to silicon, and the wall is inside.
  3. The eight outside steps. Of 3,570 ordinary steps, only eight cross, and every one is a first noble-gas core opening; each core sequence crosses inward once and stays inside.
  4. The anion rung as ω=η\omega = \eta. The wall at the zeroth rung is exactly electrophilicity equal to hardness, with 53 of 65 adopted rungs outside and a heavy-anion prediction that held 7 of 7.
  5. The colour line. All 35 metals reflect above the half-power circle and none of the 6 non-metals — the same circle as the wall on my Smith disc.
  6. The element address. Anion rung and first core opening give seven classes, with the out-and-out class lithium, boron, carbon, sodium, potassium, rubidium and caesium.
  7. The face apex as orbital survival. The textbook sudden-change overlap is exactly a function of my quarter-log face apex.
  8. The mass-ordering reversal. A signed same-charge reflection, multiplied by an anchored energy scale, predicts an increment of a measurable isobar mass difference, and holmium–dysprosium reverses order between 56+ and 57+.

Research judgements and tests before the next claim

  1. Close a measured loop. Scalar clocks on a connected network are identifiable up to one gain. Build an independently observed triangle across charge states or species, propagate shared-reference covariance, and declare a closure tolerance before acquisition. Ratios formed from the same three numbers telescope identically and only test arithmetic; an independent edge tests the premise.
  2. Test the first missing datum. Select an admissible pair matching the proposed retained ledger and varying one controlled trait: the neodymium site pair tests angular structure, the β-manganese hands test parity, and the isotope pairs test the mass anchor.
  3. Predict a response in units. A link cutoff predicts local concentration under a specified filling and partition. Keep the measured current response, localisation length, optical channel and finite-size trend separate; use a filled-band insulator and a matched metal, and record temperature, structure and probe.
  4. Complete the geometry-to-element map. An element-specific knot needs a construction from measurable configurations, or a physically fixed closure on periodic paths. Declare equivalence under cell choice and origin, and test opposite hands. Compute polynomial and mirror controls before any atomic-volume assignment; the torus-knot phase identifications in Dirac Time give a family of mathematical specimens for testing this map.
  5. Freeze genuinely new heavy tests. Hydrogen through astatine has full energy coverage in the archive. Beyond it, francium’s uncertainty spans the wall and a lone measured first ionisation energy cannot fix a two-energy opening. Element 119 is a prospective test with its call written down.
  6. Keep the losses. The heavy transfer failure, the provisional polonium miss, the failed twin equality and the scalar volume counterexample belong in the theory record. They say what information a better version has to carry.

Synthesis. The strongest physical bridge in this edition is that a signed same-charge reflection, multiplied by an externally anchored energy scale, predicts an increment of an independently measurable isobar mass difference. The strongest geometric bridge is the exact unequal-face closure, with a stated domain and falsifiable perturbations of the right-angle assumption. The weakest bridge is the step from an isolated atom’s scalar ladder to its three-dimensional occupied environment, and the programme can now say exactly which observations it lacks there. What distinguishes the work is the ability to build two systems that agree on one book and ask which further record separates them. That question stays meaningful across my papers even when a proposed identification fails.

Prior art and where this work stands

I checked what others have done before claiming anything here as new.

  • Periodic tables for ions. Lyu, Keitel and Harman (Phys. Rev. Research 7, L042071, 2025) build a periodic table for highly charged ions from the successive occupation of relativistic orbitals, with each cell an isoelectronic sequence. It is organised by orbital filling, not by a threshold on ratios of successive removal energies; it shares with my opening map the idea that an isoelectronic sequence is the natural unit. A 2026 follow-up in Atoms (14, 60) studies scaling within it.
  • Donor–acceptor maps. Pineda-Urbina (Atoms 14, 48, 2026) builds a ΔSCF-DFT donor–acceptor descriptor map for 26 main-group atoms from hydrogen to krypton, using χ=(IP+EA)/2\chi = (IP+EA)/2, η=(IP−EA)/2\eta = (IP-EA)/2, ω=μ2/2η\omega = \mu^2/2\eta and the electrodonating and electroaccepting powers. It is the closest prior art to my anion rung — the stone and the wanting — but it defines no ratio (I−A)/(I+A)(I-A)/(I+A) and no threshold; my Γ0=η/χ\Gamma_0 = \eta/\chi and the wall ω=η\omega = \eta are not in it.
  • A coordinate for within-period trends. Washburn, Simons and Allahyarov (arXiv:2605.00028, 2026) place first ionisation energy, electron affinity, Mulliken electronegativity and Pearson hardness on one noble-gas-centred axis with a golden-ratio cosh landscape function. It uses no reflection coefficient and no wall.
  • Conceptual density-functional theory. Parr and Pearson (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 105, 7512, 1983) defined absolute hardness; Parr, von Szentpály and Liu (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 121, 1922, 1999) defined the electrophilicity index ω=χ2/2η\omega = \chi^2/2\eta and ΔNmax\Delta N_{\max}. I use their definitions as a borrowed tool with their hypotheses kept, in a new domain: the borrowed quantities read my peel step. I found no published use of ω=η\omega = \eta, η/χ=1/2\eta/\chi = 1/\sqrt2 or IE/EA=3+22IE/EA = 3+2\sqrt2 as a boundary.
  • Large jumps in successive ionisation energies. That a large jump in successive ionisation energies marks the opening of a closed core is standard teaching. What is new here is a single exact threshold, derived from geometry, that separates those openings from every other step across 85 elements, and the proof that each core sequence crosses it exactly once.
  • The delocalisation sum rule. The site budget Tr(Ci−Ci2)=∑j≠i∥Pij∥2\operatorname{Tr}(C_i-C_i^2) = \sum_{j\ne i}\|P_{ij}\|^2 is the delocalisation sum rule of Bader’s atoms-in-molecules analysis and the Wiberg–Mayer bond orders; the localisation tensor is from Resta and Sorella (1999), Souza, Wilkens and Martin (2000) and Resta (2006). Dividing the nearest shell’s share by the whole budget, and reading the tensor as the integral of my intrinsic metric, are the steps I add; I found no earlier source that does them.
  • The sudden-change overlap. The 1s overlap after a sudden change of Coulomb scale is textbook atomic physics, used for electron shake-off in beta decay. The new part is that its scale coordinate is my face apex.
  • The chiral quantum walk. The three-site directional walk is Zimborás et al. (2013); here it controls a question about peeling.
  • The power–efficiency trade-off. Shiraishi, Saito and Tasaki (2016) and Pietzonka and Seifert (2018) give the trade-off between power and efficiency for heat engines; a 2026 Pareto-front analysis bounds efficiency at maximum power by half of the maximum efficiency. Elizabeth Johnson put the trade-off as “fastest or maximum energy, can’t be both”; the theorem behind it is Shiraishi–Saito–Tasaki 2016 and Pietzonka–Seifert 2018.
  • Earlier periodic tables. Russell’s octave chart (1926) and Bohr’s plate (1922) are discussed in the Russell section.
  • Data. Ionisation energies come from the NIST Atomic Spectra Database v5.12 (2024) through the pinned archive; electron affinities from Ning and Lu (2022) with the per-element updates listed in the sources.

Appendix A. The Lean certificates

Every exact statement in this paper that can be checked in finite rational arithmetic is checked in Lean 4.34.1, core library only — no Mathlib — in exact rational arithmetic. The Lean files are:

  • LoopWall.lean — 140 theorems.
  • OpeningMap.lean — 117 theorems, generated from the archive, covering all 433 noble-core openings and every ordinary ladder from scandium to astatine.
  • lean/TwoFaceForms.lean — 3 theorems (compiled on its own): two_face_identity, two_face_forms_agree (xy<(1−x)(1−y)⇔x+y<1xy<(1-x)(1-y)\iff x+y<1), two_face_forms_split_at_midpoint (at t=0.5005t = 0.5005 the pair x=0.9999x = 0.9999, y=0.0005y = 0.0005 gets different verdicts from the two forms).
  • russell/prediction_review_20261121/consistency/BoundaryAgreement.lean — 11 theorems (compiled on its own) (witnessInterior, witnessTie, witnessProduct, halfScaling, uniqueInteriorBoundary, wrongThird, midInterior, midMargins, strictCounterexample, productAntitone, rationalThreeWayControl): the all-threshold form of the two-face agreement.

Running sh run_checks.sh in lean/ builds LoopWall.lean and OpeningMap.lean with their audit files; the axiom audit prints only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for the 89 audited theorems, and the two separate files show only the same three axioms; a source scan finds no sorry, admit, native_decide or axiom. Eleven false controls are each rejected by the compiler and also proved false inside the files: carbon’s helium-core opening inside, calcium’s argon-core opening outside, fluorine’s anion rung outside, francium’s upper end inside, magnesium’s L opening outside, nitrogen’s helium-core opening outside, neon’s ratio exactly five, silicon’s anion rung inside, SS above σ\sigma with a bare hydrogen-like energy, an odd power of Γ\Gamma invariant under reversal, and the screened series outside at Z=7Z = 7. A further 61 named theorems in other self-contained research modules were replayed with the kernel checker, and the whole cross-reference hub of my work (the Work Atlas: 181 results, 80 with a linked Lean proof, across 46 repositories) updates itself from these files.

Appendix E. Sources, reproducibility and credit

Where it lives. Everything in this paper — the paper’s sources, the threshold archive, the batch records, the Lean files, the check scripts and their outputs, the review exchanges and the failed tests — is on GitHub at dicipler-pixel/votkp-lean, branch element-paper/loop-wall, folder research/2026-11-20-element-paper-loop-wall/, pinned for this edition at commit 02515d0. The interactive Periodic Table of Elemental Peels (v1.1) and its data package are deposited on Zenodo (record 24432624).

What can be checked. The 85-element inventory and the full threshold table are complete for the stated pins. All 3,655 positive-index removals and all 85 anion slots are in H_to_At_thresholds.csv, with missing affinities and missing uncertainty boxes left explicit. The element evidence is frozen at the branch commits named in the record; later amendments to the live branch belong to later editions. Each check script prints its own header and writes its output beside it. The proofs concern mathematical objects and encoded values; a reconstruction checks code against source; a measured comparison needs independent experimental information. Agreement between two scripts reading the same NIST-derived input checks the transformation, not the underlying spectroscopic measurement.

Coverage boundary. The companion batch files hold material properties, spectra, nuclear cases and crystal phases with uneven coverage. No claim is made of an exhaustive evaluated handbook of every isotope, phase, pressure, thermal history and optical band for all 85 elements. No universal element-to-knot assignment, nuclear decay rate, bulk transport law or experimental realisation of an elementary knot follows from this edition. Radon onward, the final polonium uncertainty budget and francium’s second ionisation energy remain open.

My own sources. The Dirac Time of the Gigantefermion, long form v3.0.1 (25 September 2026) and v3.1 (26 September 2026); VOTKP: The Vector of Traits Kept under Peeling, v2.9 (13 October 2026) and the v3.0–v3.3 editions (12 November 2026); The Volume of the Knot Potential: Decay and Direction on the Vacuum Disk (7 November 2026, and v6); Two Trees in One Ball v4; Intrinsic Quantum Geometric Tensor (v7.3); Universal Projector Geometry from Electrical Measurements (v3.2); Non-Normality Is Connection Energy (Zenodo concept 10.5281/zenodo.22803572); The Offset Belongs to the Boundary (v31); What Transport Keeps (edition 3); The Offset Speed Limit and The Weight Between (v1.1, 26 October 2026); The Ledger Outlives the Metric (final edition v3 and edition 6); Matter at a Scale (v5); What Russell Saw (26 September 2026) and Russell, Corrected (3 November 2026); A Five-Dimensional Non-Normal Stability Operator with Gradient-Driven Interface Coupling for Zero-Precursor Filamentary Fractures (17 September 2026); Foundational Operator Field Theory on Stratified Manifolds v2 (August 2026); Colour Selects the Leader v1.2 (2 November 2026, doi 10.5281/zenodo.23876186); the ball folders on the moving-matrix branch; my November working notes and harness records.
